title: Robo and the Sleepy Moon
story:
One quiet night on Moon Base, Robo looked up and gasped. The moon's big glow lamp had gone dim! Without it, the little space islands were too dark to see.

Robo zoomed up on his jet boots. He hovered over a crater, then another, then a wobbly floating rock. At the very top sat the glow lamp, flickering like a sleepy firefly.

"Hmm," said Robo, tapping his antenna. "Maybe you just need a friend." He hummed the Robo Jump song very softly. Beep, boop, bee-doo! The lamp blinked. It wiggled. Then it glowed bright and happy again, as if it had been lonely up there all by itself.

From then on, Robo flew up every night to hum the lamp a song. And Moon Base glowed softly all night long, cozy as a nightlight.

title: The Blinky Block Who Wanted to Stay
story:
Far away in Glitch Galaxy, Robo was hopping home when he landed on a blinky block. Blink! It vanished. Blink! It came back. Robo wobbled and laughed. "Sorry!" squeaked the block. "I can't stop blinking. All the other blocks stay still, and I keep disappearing."

Robo sat down on the next block and thought hard, his blue eyes glowing. "You know what? When you blink, you make a little game. Jumping on you is the most fun part of this whole galaxy!"

The block blinked a happy blink. Then it had an idea. It called its blinky friends, and they lined up into a twinkly path pointing straight toward home. Blink, hop. Blink, hop. Robo bounced all the way across.

"Thank you!" he waved. And the blinky blocks blinked goodnight, proud to be exactly the way they were.

title: Duke Googool's Cold Tea
story:
Duke Googool sat in his Goo Mech, sipping tea, with a frown under his monocle. "Bother," he sighed. "My tea is always cold. Being sneaky takes so long that it never stays warm."

Robo landed nearby with a goo grapple swing. He had come for a Star Engine, but he could see the Duke looked glum. "What's wrong?" Robo asked. "Cold tea," said the Duke. "Every single day."

Robo had an idea. He held the little cup up to a glowing Star Engine. In just a moment, the tea was warm and toasty. The Duke took a sip and his top hat wiggled with joy.

"Oh my! Perhaps," he said slowly, "stars are better for sharing than stealing." So the Duke gave back the Star Engines, and every Sunday after that, Robo came over for warm tea and goo cookies.

title: Two Visors, One Puzzle
story:
Nega-Robo had turned another world into a mirror copy. Left was right, up was down, and even the clouds were backwards. Robo scratched his round white head. "How do I get through this?"

He tried Rocket Robo. Whoosh! He flew the wrong way. He tried Drill Robo. Brrr! He drilled up into the sky. Silly! Then he saw Nega-Robo sitting on a mirror ledge, red visor drooping. "I made it too confusing," Nega-Robo grumbled. "Now even I can't find the way out."

Robo held out his hand. "Then let's figure it out together. You know the mirror. I know the real world." Robo turned into Bubble Robo, and Nega-Robo pointed the way. They floated past every backwards cloud.

At the exit, Nega-Robo almost smiled. "Maybe a twin is better as a teammate." Robo giggled. "That's what I've been saying!"

title: The Littlest Bot Buddy
story:
Inside the Game Factory computer, Robo was tiny as a crumb. He had rescued fifty-nine bot buddies, but one was still missing. Where could it be?

He checked the keyboard world. He peeked under a mouse cursor. He even tiptoed past the snoring Blue Screen Blob. No bot buddy anywhere.

Then Robo heard a tiny "beep" coming from the Memory Museum. There, curled up next to a Game Memory of Ben's very first game, was the littlest bot buddy of all. "I didn't want to leave," it whispered. "This memory is my favorite."

Robo smiled. "Then you can be the museum's helper! You'll keep every memory shiny and safe." The little bot beamed brighter than a pixel. Now, whenever Ben makes a new game, a tiny bot buddy dusts off its memory and hangs it on the wall with care.

title: The Phantom Pancake Breakfast
story:
After the big adventure, Moon Base was fixed and shiny again. King Gloop had a happy idea. "Let's have a pancake breakfast for the whole team!"

But oh no! Every pancake kept flying off the pan and dashing through the walls. Whoosh! Whoosh! They had picked up a little phantom power from the Phantom Core. Baby Gloop giggled and chased one. Duke Googool tried to catch one with his top hat. Nega-Robo grabbed a plate and missed. The pancakes zipped everywhere!

Robo had an idea. He did his own phantom dash, right through the wall, and stood still holding a big bottle of syrup. The pancakes stopped. They sniffed. Then plop, plop, plop, they landed in a tall stack on his plate.

Everyone cheered. They sat around the table, sticky and happy, and agreed it was the best breakfast in the whole galaxy.

title: The Golden Bit's Lost Song
story:
In the remixed worlds of the Glitch Factory, Robo found a Golden Bit sitting all alone. It was humming, but the tune kept skipping. "La, la, beep... la, glitch!" "I used to know the whole song," said the Golden Bit sadly. "But the glitch mixed it up."

Robo called his friends. Phantom Robo remembered the first part. King Gloop remembered the middle, which was mostly wobbly. Baby Gloop knew the bouncy bit, and Duke Googool remembered the fancy ending, of course.

One by one, they sang their pieces in the right order. The Golden Bit glowed brighter with every note. When the last note rang out, the song was whole again!

The Golden Bit sparkled and flew up into Robo's backpack. "Thank you," it chimed. And all the way home, it hummed its song without a single skip.

title: A Dinosaur Who Needed a Hat
story:
Way back in Dino Time, Robo was sneaking along in his Retro Camo when he heard a big sniffle. A gentle green dinosaur was sitting under a palm tree. "The sun is so hot," it sighed. "And I have no hat."

Robo looked around. Leaves, rocks, a very surprised beetle. Then he had an idea. He gathered giant palm leaves and wove them together, just like a basket. Snip, tuck, fold!

He hopped up onto the dinosaur's nose and placed the leafy hat on top. It was a perfect fit. The dinosaur's tail wagged so hard it made a breeze through the whole jungle.

"Thank you, little shiny friend!" it rumbled. Then it gave Robo a ride all the way to the next Time Portal. Robo waved goodbye, and the dinosaur waved back, wearing its hat proudly.

title: Laserheart Learns to Share
story:
When Robo finally zipped home to Moon Base, it was very quiet. The only one there was Laserheart, glowing pink and making clone after clone of itself.

"Why so many clones?" Robo asked gently. Laserheart's glow flickered. "Because Moon Base was empty. I didn't want to be alone, so I made friends out of me."

Robo understood. He had been zipping alone too, and it had felt very lonely. "Then let's fill it with real friends," he said. He sent a message across the galaxy, and soon King Gloop, Baby Gloop, Duke Googool and Nega-Robo came zooming home.

Laserheart was shy at first. But Baby Gloop handed Laserheart a cookie, and its glow turned the warmest pink ever. The clones waved goodbye and blinked away. Moon Base was full again, and nobody had to be alone.

title: The Key That Fit Everything
story:
Lock Robo had put padlocks on every game in the Game Factory book. Robo and his friends found key pieces all over, from Ninja Cat's rooftops to Turbo Racers' race track. But when they put the pieces together, the key was wobbly and would not turn.

"Hmm," said Robo. "Maybe something is missing." They went to see Lock Robo, who sat on a giant padlock looking grumpy. "Why lock everything?" Robo asked. "Because everyone has a page except me," said Lock Robo quietly.

Robo looked at the key, then at Lock Robo. "What if the missing piece is you?" Lock Robo touched the key, and click! It glowed and turned in every lock at once.

All the games burst open with happy music. And on the very next page, a brand-new spot appeared, just for Lock Robo, with a little padlock drawing and a big smiley face.

title: Spinning Round the Islands
story:
On the floating space islands, everything was real 3D. Robo could walk forward, back, and all around. But one little island was spinning too fast. Round and round it went, like a top!

A family of space bunnies lived on that island. They were very, very dizzy. "Help!" they squeaked. "We can't stop twirling!"

Robo took a big jump and landed right in the middle. Whirrr! He was dizzy too. Then he noticed the island had a little wheel underneath, turning in the wind. Robo grabbed a floating cloud and tucked it in front of the wheel like a pillow. The wind stopped pushing. The island slowed down, then stopped.

The space bunnies wobbled, giggled and hugged Robo's legs. That night they had a carrot party, and the island stayed perfectly still, except when everyone danced.

title: The Level That Built Itself a Friend
story:
In Robo Builder, Ben had made a brand-new level, full of blocks, bugs and warps. But one little block at the end felt left out. Nobody ever jumped on it, because the goal flag was just before it.

"I wish someone would visit me," it sighed. That night, after the screen went quiet, Robo hopped into the level to practice. He bounced across the blocks, zipped through a warp, and reached the flag. Then he heard the tiny sigh.

Robo looked past the flag. "Oh! Hello there!" He carefully moved the flag one step over, so the little block was now the very last jump before the finish.

The next day, everyone who played the level landed on that block right before winning. It felt so proud. It even got a nickname: The Victory Block.

title: The Crate That Was Shy
story:
Deep in the glitch maze, Robo needed to push a crate onto a big shiny switch. He pushed. It didn't move. He pushed harder. It scooted back! "Excuse me," said a tiny voice. It was the crate. "I'm scared of that switch. It makes a loud CLUNK."

Robo knelt down. "That's okay. Loud sounds can be scary." He thought for a moment. Then he found a fluffy cushion in a corner of the maze, and laid it right on top of the switch.

"Now it will make a soft little poof," Robo said. "Want to try?"

The crate slid forward very slowly. It rolled onto the switch and went, poof! The door opened with a happy jingle. The crate giggled. "That was fun!" They finished all fifteen puzzles together, and the crate was never shy again.

title: The Alien Who Was Just Lost
story:
Robo was flying over Moon Base with his laser blaster when he spotted one small alien ship that wasn't attacking. It was zigzagging, bumping into stars, and beeping sadly.

Robo flew closer. A tiny green alien waved from the window. "I'm sorry!" it called. "I'm not here to fight. I got lost following the big ships, and now I can't find my way home!"

Robo lowered his blaster. "Do you have a map?" The alien held up a crumpled paper. It was upside down! Robo turned it the right way, and the alien gasped. "Oh! Home is that way!"

To say thank you, the little alien gave Robo a glowing pebble from its planet. Robo put it on his shelf at Moon Base. And every night, when it twinkled, he knew his new friend had made it home safe.

title: The Robot With Mismatched Socks
story:
In Robo Workshop, Ben built a brand-new robot. It had a square head, one spring arm, one claw arm, a rolling wheel and a jumping leg. It was painted every color at once. The robot looked at the other robots in the Battle Tower. They all matched. "Am I built wrong?" it wondered.

At the first floor, a boss robot blocked the stairs and stomped. The new robot tried to stomp back, but it only had one leg. So it bounced on its spring instead, boing, boing, right over the boss's head!

At the next floor, it rolled under a laser with its wheel. At the next, it grabbed a key with its claw. Every mixed-up part was perfect for something.

At the top of the tower, the robot looked in a shiny mirror and smiled. "I'm not built wrong. I'm built just right for me."

title: The Banana Peel Picnic
story:
At Kart Party, Robo, Sparks, Pages and all their pals were zooming around the track. Everyone was throwing banana peels, and soon the road was so slippery that every kart was spinning in circles!

Whee! Wobble! Bonk! Nobody could finish the race. Robo stopped his kart and looked at the giant pile of peels. "We need to clean these up," he said. "But what do we do with so many?"

Pages the cat had an idea. "Where there are peels, there were bananas! Who ate them all?" Everyone looked at King Gloop, who had a very full tummy and a sheepish grin.

So they cleared the track together, put all the peels in the compost bin, and made a promise: one banana each, no more throwing. Then they raced again, and everyone crossed the finish line laughing, with King Gloop in last place, happily munching a snack.

title: When the Villains Took a Day Off
story:
Factory Battle was a busy place. Heroes from every game fought villains from the other games, all day long. But one morning, every villain in the Villain Tower stayed in bed.

"We're tired," yawned a big boss. "Being bad all the time is exhausting." The heroes didn't know what to do. Robo scratched his antenna. Captain Woof wagged his tail. Then Sammy the cat said, "Sweet freedom! Let's have a day off too!"

So everyone had a picnic in the factory yard instead. Heroes and villains shared sandwiches. A goo monster taught Robo a new dance. Even The Factory Glitch came down and played tag, though it kept flickering to the wrong spot.

At sunset, everyone agreed the battles could start again tomorrow. But they also made a new rule: one picnic day every week, for everyone.

title: Charlie and August Take a Wrong Turn
story:
Charlie and August, the two cats who drive Sparks the robot dog, were on a kitten rescue. Charlie steered and August pushed the buttons. Sparks wagged his long purple tail.

But oops! August pressed the wrong button. Sparks spun around and trotted into a field of tall sunflowers. Now they couldn't see anything but yellow petals!

"We're lost," said Charlie. "Maybe not," said August. "Sparks has the best nose in three books!" August pressed the SNIFF button. Sparks lifted his yellow snout. Sniff, sniff, sniff! Then he wagged and trotted straight through the flowers.

On the other side, they found a tiny kitten stuck in a teacup. Charlie scooped it up, August gave it a cuddle, and Sparks gave a happy beep-bark. The wrong turn had been the right turn after all.

title: Snatcher and the Donut Dilemma
story:
Snatcher, the sneaky cat, had taken every donut in town. Again! Captain Woof glided down on his cape and landed with a heroic woof.

"Snatcher! Why do you keep taking the donuts?" Snatcher hugged the big box and looked away. "Because nobody ever invites me to donut time."

Captain Woof's ears drooped. He hadn't known that. He thought about his BARK BLAST. Then he thought about kindness instead. "Well," he said, "would you like to come to donut time tomorrow? Right after you give these back?" Snatcher blinked. "Really? Me?"

The next morning, the whole town sat at a long table. There were sprinkle donuts, jelly donuts and one big one shaped like a cape. Snatcher sat right next to Captain Woof, purring. And for once, nobody needed a hero at all.

title: King Snickers Can't Sleep
story:
In the castle, King Snickers tossed and turned in his royal cat bed. "I can't sleep," he meowed. "It's too quiet now that Grim the Bone Lord has gone away."

The cat butler brought warm milk. It didn't help. The cat butler fluffed the pillows. Still not sleepy.

Then Feathers the bird flew in through the window. "I know what you need!" she chirped. She grabbed a little bell in her beak and flew to the top of the tower. Then she pulled the lever for the castle music box.

Ting, ting, ting. A soft, sleepy song floated through the halls. The cat butler hummed along. King Snickers yawned a big royal yawn. "Perfect," he whispered. Feathers tucked herself onto the bedpost, and soon the whole castle was snoring gently, all the way till morning.

title: The Ball That Wanted to Try Everything
story:
At Sports Party, there were five games: baseball, basketball, soccer, mini golf and football. Each game had its own ball. But one little bouncy ball didn't have a game. "I want to play too!" it squeaked.

It tried baseball, but it was too bouncy and flew over the fence. It tried basketball, but it was too small and fell right through the net. It tried soccer, but it rolled away under a bench.

Then it bounced over to mini golf. It rolled up the ramp, around the windmill and plop, right into the hole. Hole in one!

All the other balls cheered. The golf ball scooted over and said, "You can be my partner!" From that day on, the little bouncy ball played mini golf every afternoon. And sometimes, just for fun, it still tried to dunk.

title: The Dragon King's Birthday
story:
The hero of Ben's Quest had a shiny sword and the temple key. But when the hero reached the Dragon King's cave, it was decorated with streamers. The Dragon King was sitting alone with a tiny cake.

"It's my birthday," the dragon rumbled. "Nobody ever comes. They just want to fight me." The hero put down the sword. "Then I'll stay for cake!"

The hero ran back through the forest and invited everyone: the village baker, the friendly slimes, even the guards from the temple. They came marching up the hill with presents and candles.

The Dragon King was so happy that he blew out his candles with a gentle puff of warm air, and nothing caught fire at all. Everyone sang. And from then on, the Dragon King was the friendliest dragon in the whole kingdom.

title: Zoomy's Slowest Race
story:
Zoomy, Speedy and Rocket were the fastest racers on all three tracks. They loved the boost arrows. Zoom! Whoosh! Vroom!

But one day, during the big race, Zoomy saw a family of ducks crossing the road. A mama duck and five little ducklings, waddling very slowly.

Zoomy hit the brakes. Screech! Speedy stopped too. Then Rocket. All three racers sat and waited, engines humming softly, while the ducklings took their time. Waddle, waddle, waddle, quack. The crowd was quiet. Then they started cheering louder than ever. "Hooray for the kind racers!"

When the ducks were safe, the three cars finished the race side by side. Nobody won first place. But the judges gave all of them a shiny trophy that said Best Racers Ever. Zoomy kept it right next to the boost arrows.

title: The House With No Door
story:
In Build It!, the builders made a beautiful house. It had big windows, a red roof, a pool and even a doghouse. A family of little people moved in, along with a happy dog.

But the next morning, nobody could get outside! The builders had forgotten something important: a front door! The dog barked at the wall. The people looked out the windows and waved. "Hello? We would like to go for a walk!"

The builders laughed at their silly mistake. They grabbed their tools and carefully cut out a door shape. They added a doorknob, a welcome mat and a little bell. Ding-dong!

The family stepped outside and took a big breath of fresh air. The dog ran three happy circles around the pool. And the builders added one more thing on top of the house: a sign that said Never Forget the Door.

title: Brawl Buddies Bake-Off
story:
Robo Max, Ninja Kit, Dino Rex and Wizard Zap battled every day. But today, the arena was closed for cleaning. "What should we do?" asked Dino Rex, swinging his tail. "Let's have a bake-off instead!" said Wizard Zap.

Robo Max mixed batter super fast with his robot arms. Ninja Kit sliced strawberries with lightning speed. Dino Rex stomped so hard the oven door popped open. Wizard Zap waved his wand to make the frosting sparkle.

But oh no, the cake was a disaster! It was lumpy, leaning and covered in sparkles. They all looked at it and burst out laughing. Then Dino Rex took a big bite. "Mmm! It's delicious!"

They shared every crumb. And they agreed that a lumpy cake made with friends is better than any trophy.

title: The Zombie Who Wanted a Bath
story:
In the Zombie Maze, the explorer had found three treasure chests. Just one more to go! Then a slow, shuffling zombie stepped out from behind a wall. The explorer got a water balloon ready.

But the zombie held up its hands. "Wait! Please splash me!" The explorer blinked. "You want to get splashed?" "Yes!" groaned the zombie. "I'm all dusty, and it's sooo itchy. Those water balloons feel like a nice cool shower."

So the explorer threw balloon after balloon. Splash! Splash! The zombie twirled and laughed. Soon it was clean and shiny, and it smelled like lemon soap.

To say thank you, the zombie pointed down a secret hallway. There sat the fourth treasure chest, glittering with gold. The explorer escaped the maze, and the zombie waved goodbye, fresh and happy at last.

title: Champion Juniper's Lost Monster
story:
At the top of Ember Peak, Champion Juniper looked worried. "Have you seen my little fire monster?" she asked. "It wandered off this morning." The Monster Pals trainer wanted to help. They searched the tall grass, the misty lake and the sleepy cave. No little fire monster anywhere.

Then the trainer had an idea. "Fire monsters like warm places. Where's the warmest spot around?" They looked at each other and smiled. "The bakery!"

They hurried down the mountain. Sure enough, the little fire monster was curled up next to the bakery oven, sound asleep, with a cinnamon roll in its paws.

Juniper laughed and scooped it up. "Thank you, Champion! You found my friend." Then she bought cinnamon rolls for everyone, and all the monsters shared a warm, sweet snack by the oven.

title: The Bunny Who Wouldn't Hop
story:
At Pet Park, every pet loved learning tricks. The puppy could sit. The kitten could spin. But one fluffy bunny just sat in the corner, nose twitching. "Why won't you hop?" asked the park helper kindly.

The bunny looked at the bubble bath area. "I'm scared I'll hop into the bubbles by accident." The helper smiled. "Let's make a special hopping path, far away from the bubbles." They laid out soft mats in a line across the grass. They put a carrot at the very end.

The bunny looked at the carrot. It looked at the mats. Then it took one tiny hop. Then another. Then hop, hop, HOP, all the way to the carrot!

All the other pets cheered. The bunny was so proud that it hopped all afternoon. And it even tried one little bubble bath, just to see. It loved it.

title: The Color That Got Lost
story:
In Paint Studio, all the colors lived happily in their little paint pots. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. But one morning, the purple pot was empty!

"Where did Purple go?" asked Yellow. The colors searched every coloring page. They looked under the stamps and behind the rainbow brush. No Purple anywhere.

Then Red and Blue bumped into each other by accident. Swish! Where they touched, a lovely purple swirl appeared. The colors gasped. "Purple was never lost," said Blue with a smile. "Purple is made from us!"

Red and Blue mixed and mixed until the purple pot was full again. Purple stretched and giggled. "Thanks for finding me!" And that day, the sparkle brush painted a giant rainbow across the page, with Purple shining right at the top.

title: The Planet That Forgot How to Count
story:
Math Rocket zoomed toward the ninth planet, the hardest one of all. But when it landed, the aliens there looked very confused.

"We forgot how to count!" said the alien mayor. "We don't know how many moons we have, or how many cookies to bake for our party." The pilot climbed out with a big smile. "I can help! Counting is my favorite."

They pointed at the sky together. "One moon, two moons, three moons!" They counted the guests. "Ten aliens, plus two more coming late. That makes twelve!" So they baked twelve cookies, and one extra for the pilot.

The aliens cheered and danced. They made a big poster with all the numbers on it so they would never forget again. And before the rocket flew home, they counted down together: "Five, four, three, two, one, blast off!"

title: The Alien Who Didn't Like Cheese
story:
On the space station, the pizza shop was busy. Aliens lined up for pizzas with moon cheese, star sauce and comet pepperoni. But one small purple alien sat at the counter with a sad face.

"I'm allergic to cheese," it said. "I've never had pizza." The pizza chef thought hard. Then the chef rolled out the dough, spread on extra star sauce, and added crunchy space peppers, sweet galaxy pineapple and little crater mushrooms. No cheese at all.

The pizza came out of the oven, warm and colorful. The little alien took a bite. Its antennae wiggled with joy. "This is the best thing I've ever eaten!"

From then on, the shop had a new pizza on the menu. It was called the Cosmic Rainbow, and it was the most popular pizza in the whole galaxy.

title: The Silly Monsters' Secret
story:
Every day, the silly monsters marched toward the castle. The archer towers, cannon towers, ice towers and lightning towers stopped them every time. But they kept coming back! One day, the castle keeper climbed down and asked, "Why do you keep marching here?"

The biggest silly monster wiggled its ears. "We just want to see the castle garden. We heard it has the best flowers in the land." The keeper laughed so hard her crown slipped. "Is that all? You could have knocked!"

So she opened the big castle gates. The silly monsters tiptoed in very carefully. They smelled the roses, the daisies and the giant sunflowers. One monster cried happy tears.

After that, the towers took a nap every Saturday. That was garden day, and the silly monsters always brought a little gift: a pebble, a feather, or a very silly hat.

title: Pages Finds a Bookmark
story:
Pages the cat loved running through the Game Factory book. Page after page, game after game. But every night, Pages forgot which page was the last one visited.

"I always have to start from the beginning," Pages sighed, curling up on the cover. Robo walked by and noticed. "You need a bookmark!" he said.

They searched through the book for something just right. A feather from Feathers the bird was too tickly. A Golden Bit was too shiny. Then they found a long, soft ribbon on the Paint Studio page, striped with every color.

Robo tied it gently into the book. Pages stretched out right on top of it, like a cozy blanket. "Now I'll always know where I stopped." From then on, every night, Pages tucked the ribbon in, purred softly and fell asleep right where the adventure left off.

title: The Hero in the Wrong Game
story:
In the Glitch Factory, everything was mixed up. Sammy the cat was in Math Rocket. A racing car was in Paint Studio. And Robo was stuck inside Pet Park, wearing a bunny collar!

"This is silly," Robo laughed. "But I need to fix it." He found the glitch hiding behind a bubble bath. It was a small, buzzy square of static, and it looked worried. "I didn't mean to mix things up," it fizzed. "I just sneezed!"

Robo smiled. "Everybody sneezes. Let's put things back together." The glitch hopped on Robo's shoulder and pointed out each mixed-up hero. One by one, they sent Sammy, the car and everyone else back to their own pages.

When the last hero was home, the glitch gave a tiny, happy buzz. Robo gave it a tissue, just in case. And the Game Factory was all fixed, with only one giggle left over.

title: The Question Nobody Could Answer
story:
On the Game Factory Quiz show, the host had a special question. "What is the very best game in the whole Game Factory?"

The buzzers went quiet. Robo thought it was Robo Jump. Sammy thought it was Sammy's Day. King Gloop thought it was Gloop Bowling, because it had his name in it.

"Hmm," said the host. "Everyone has a different answer." The contestants started to argue. "Mine!" "No, mine!" "Gloop Bowling!" It got very loud. Then a little voice from the audience spoke up. "Maybe the best game is the one you're playing with friends."

Everyone stopped. They looked at each other and smiled. The host checked the answer card and flipped it over. In big letters, it said: ALL OF THEM. Everybody got the points. The confetti cannon went off, and they all shared the prize, a giant bowl of popcorn.

title: The Sound That Couldn't Be Guessed
story:
In Guess It!, there was a sound quiz. Players heard a sound and guessed which game it came from. A boing was Robo Jump. A meow was Sammy. A splat was King Gloop.

But one sound was a mystery. It went, "hmmmm-hmmmm-hmm." Nobody could guess it! Not Robo. Not the Gloops. Not even Duke Googool, who knew everything. They listened again. Hmmmm-hmmmm-hmm. "Is it a fridge?" asked Baby Gloop. "A bee?" asked Robo.

Then they followed the sound down the hallway, around the corner and into the quiz room's back closet. There sat the quiz machine itself, humming happily to its own song.

"That's me!" it said. "I was just so happy to have so many friends playing." Everyone laughed. They added a new question to the quiz: What sound does a happy quiz make?

title: The Note That Was Always Late
story:
At Beat Party, the music notes slid down the screen and landed in the circles right on the beat. Tap, tap, tap! But one little note was always late. Its friends would land, and then it would plop in a moment after.

"I'm sorry," it said. "I'm just a bit slower." The other notes frowned. The song sounded a little bumpy. Then the bass note had an idea. "What if you're not late? What if you're an echo?"

They tried the song again. Tap, tap, tap... and then the little note landed, soft and sweet. Tap. It sounded like the song was singing back to itself!

Everyone in the party cheered. It was the coolest sound they had ever heard. From then on, the little note had a special job in Song Maker. It was the Echo Note, and every song wanted one.

title: King Gloop's Impossible Order
story:
At the Candy Factory, orders came in all day. Robo wanted rocket fuel lollipops. Sparks wanted bone-shaped gummies. Then King Gloop wobbled up with a very special order. "I want a candy that tastes like ALL the flavors at once!"

The candy maker scratched her head. Strawberry, lemon, chocolate, mint, even pickle? All at once? The machine beeped nervously. The candy maker tried mixing every flavor into one candy. It came out brown and lumpy. Yuck. She tried again. This time it exploded into sprinkles. Oops!

Then she had a clever idea. She made tiny candies in every flavor and stacked them in a tall rainbow tower, one on top of the other. "You can taste them all, one bite at a time!"

King Gloop took a bite from the top all the way to the bottom. "Delicious! Even the pickle!"

title: The Bot Who Did Everyone's Tasks
story:
In Sus Factory, fifteen robots ran around doing their tasks. Fix the wires. Clean the vents. Water the plants. But one little robot was doing everybody's tasks! The other robots called a meeting. "That's sus!" said a red bot. "Why would anyone do so many tasks?"

They all looked at the little robot. It shuffled its feet. "Well, I'm brand new. I wanted everyone to like me. So I tried to help a lot."

The red bot's antenna drooped. "Oh. We thought you were the sneaky bot." "No," said the little robot. "I'm just a helpful bot."

The robots felt bad for being so suspicious. They gave the little robot a big welcome sticker. Then they made a rule: everybody does their own tasks, and if you finish early, you help a friend. Nobody needed to vote anyone out that day.

title: Evil Sparks Learns to Wag
story:
Down in the Evil Game Factory, everything was dark and grumpy. Evil Sparks was the grumpiest of all. He growled at the clouds. He growled at the gears. He even growled at his own tail.

When Robo arrived, Evil Sparks growled at him too. But Robo noticed something. Evil Sparks's tail was trying to wag, just a little. "Do you like playing fetch?" Robo asked. "Evil dogs don't play fetch," growled Evil Sparks. But his tail wagged a tiny bit more.

Robo found an old ball in the corner, wiped off the dust, and tossed it. It bounced down the hall. Evil Sparks tried to stay still. Tried really hard. Then he zoomed after it!

When he came back, ball in mouth, his tail was wagging so fast it made a breeze. And right then, a little light switched on in the Evil Factory. It was starting to turn good.

title: The Magma King's Cold Toes
story:
At the very top of the volcano factory, the Magma King sat on his rocky throne. All day long, he made the lava bubble higher and higher.

Robo climbed up, puffing and sweaty. "Why do you keep making the lava rise?" he asked. The Magma King looked down. "Because my toes are cold," he grumbled. "The lava is the only warm thing here."

Robo looked at the king's big rocky feet. They really did look chilly. Then Robo had an idea. He grabbed the softest thing in his backpack, a pair of thick red socks from the Snow Factory.

He helped the Magma King pull them on. They stretched and stretched, but they fit! The king wiggled his toes and sighed happily. "So toasty!" The lava calmed down and went back to a gentle bubble. And Robo flew home on his rocket, waving to a very cozy king.

title: The Smallest Scare Bug
story:
In the Scare Factory, the lights were out and the glowing Scare Bugs zoomed around. Robo zapped them one by one, and they floated back to their home in the garden.

But one Scare Bug was too tiny to scare anyone. It glowed a soft little green, like a firefly. It hid behind a machine and trembled.

"You don't have to be scared," Robo said gently. "I won't zap you." "I'm a Scare Bug who isn't scary," it whispered. "The Queen will be so disappointed." Robo looked at its gentle glow. "But you make a really nice nightlight." The tiny bug blinked.

When Robo fixed the last machine, the factory lights came back on. But Robo asked the tiny bug to stay in the hallway, just in case anyone woke up in the night. It glowed softly by the door, proud to be the factory's very own nightlight.

title: The Snowman Who Wanted to See Summer
story:
In the Snow Factory, Robo built the most wonderful snowman. It had a carrot nose, button eyes and a little scarf. Its name was Flurry.

Flurry looked out the factory window at the green hills. "I wish I could see summer," it said. "But I'd melt!" Robo thought and thought. Sparks barked. Pages licked a paw. Then the Snow-O-Matic gave a happy whirr, and Robo got an idea.

They put Flurry in a little wagon with a tiny Snow-O-Matic on the back. It puffed out cool snowflakes all over Flurry like a mini snowstorm. Then they rolled outside together.

Flurry saw butterflies, bright flowers and a big yellow sun, all while staying perfectly frosty. "Summer is beautiful!" it cheered. Then they rolled home before dinner, and Flurry told every snowman all about it.

title: The Clone Who Picked Its Own Name
story:
In the Clone Factory, Robo used his Good Beam to turn the wild clones good. There were icy clones, speedy clones, tiny clones and one giant clone. Soon he had a whole Robo Army.

But one tiny clone looked sad. "Everybody is called Robo," it said. "How will anyone know which one is me?" Robo knelt down. "You're right. You should have your own name. What do you like?"

The tiny clone thought. "I like bubbles. And bouncing. And the color green." "How about Bubbo?" said Robo. The tiny clone's visor lit up. "Bubbo! I love it!"

Soon every clone was picking a name. There was Zippy, Frosty, Big Biscuit and one called Mr. Wobbles. King Gloop wrote them all on name tags. And Bubbo wore its tag every single day, right on its tiny shiny chest.

title: Chaos Nova's Wish
story:
At the very end of The Final Factory, after every boss had been beaten, Chaos Nova floated in the sky. The rainbow star glowed bright, and its one big eye blinked slowly.

"Why do you want to beat the Game Factory?" Robo asked. Chaos Nova was quiet for a long time. Then it said, "Because I wanted to be part of the story. I didn't know how else to get in."

Robo understood. Being left out is a very hard feeling. "You don't have to be a boss to be in the story," he said. "You can just be a friend." Chaos Nova's rainbow shimmered. "Really?"

When the longest credits ever rolled across the screen, there was one extra name at the very end. It said: And our friend, Chaos Nova. The rainbow star twinkled so brightly that the whole factory glowed.

title: Sir Wobblebottom's Big Day
story:
In Boss Builder, someone made a brand-new boss. It had a goo body, googly eyes, butterfly wings, a tiny crown and the size setting turned all the way up to GIGANTIC. Its silly name was Sir Wobblebottom.

Sir Wobblebottom looked at its three attacks: the Bubble Burp, the Tickle Wing and the Big Bounce. "Hmm," it said. "These aren't very scary." It worried all morning. What if nobody wanted to fight it?

Then the first player arrived. Sir Wobblebottom did a Bubble Burp. The player giggled! It did a Tickle Wing. The player laughed so hard they fell over. It did a Big Bounce and the whole arena wobbled like jelly.

The player won, but they were smiling ear to ear. "That was the funniest boss ever!" Sir Wobblebottom blushed bright pink. Being silly, it decided, was its very best superpower.

title: The Dancer Who Was Off the Beat
story:
In Music Videos, all the characters danced together. Robo spun. King Gloop wiggled. Sammy did a flip. Everyone moved to the beat, step, step, clap!

Everyone except Baby Gloop. Baby Gloop clapped when everyone stepped, and stepped when everyone clapped. Plop, oops, plop! "I'll never get it right," Baby Gloop sniffled. Robo stopped the music. "Let's try something. You listen to the song, and show us YOUR dance."

Baby Gloop closed its eyes and listened. Then it began to sway, slow and wobbly, like jelly in the wind. It was nothing like the others. But it was beautiful.

Robo started copying Baby Gloop. Then Sammy did. Then everyone! They called it the Gloopy Sway. It became the most popular move in the whole Hyper Factory remix, and Baby Gloop got to lead it every time.

title: The Factory Heart's Lullaby
story:
It was a spooky night in the factories. Robo had bonked every boss, from the Candy Machine to Mecha Robo. Now there was just one left: The Factory Heart, which pumped power to everything.

But when Robo reached it, the Factory Heart wasn't scary at all. It was beating very fast, thump-thump-thump-thump.

"I can't calm down," it said. "I've been working all day and all night. I've never had a rest." Robo sat down beside it. He thought about how he felt at bedtime. Then, very softly, he hummed the Robo Jump song, slow and sleepy.

Thump-thump. Thump... thump. The Factory Heart began to glow a soft, warm gold. It beat slower and slower, steady and calm. "Thank you," it whispered. All the factories went quiet and cozy. Even the spooky night felt peaceful now, like a big, warm blanket over everything.

title: Costume Mix-Up
story:
In the Holiday Song Room, Robo and his friends had a costume for every holiday. Pumpkins for Halloween. Santa hats for Christmas. Bunny ears for Easter. But one day, the costume closet tipped over!

Costumes flew everywhere. When everyone got dressed for the Valentine's song, Robo wore a pumpkin, King Gloop wore bunny ears, and Sammy wore a party hat from New Year's.

"Oh no!" said Robo. "We're all wrong!" But the music had already started. So they danced anyway. Pumpkin Robo twirled. Bunny Gloop bounced. Party Sammy did a dramatic spin.

When the song ended, everyone was laughing so hard they couldn't stop. The audience loved it. So they invented a brand-new holiday right then and there: Silly Mix-Up Day, when everybody wears the wrong costume and dances to every song.

title: The Rule Nobody Expected
story:
In Mystery Mix, the Mix Wheel spun every thirty seconds. Upside-down screen! Flipped gravity! Giant Robo! Robo laughed his way through every silly rule. But one day, the wheel got stuck. It creaked and clicked and wouldn't spin.

"Uh oh," said Robo. "No more silly rules?" He looked closer. A little gear inside the wheel was tired and squeaky. Robo got some oil from his backpack and gave it a gentle drop. Then he gave the wheel a friendly push.

The wheel spun faster than ever, and it landed on a rule nobody had ever seen. It said: EVERYBODY HUGS!

Robo blinked. Then every star in the level floated over and hugged him. The platforms hugged each other. Even the slippery ice gave a chilly little squeeze. It was the best rule yet, and the Mix Wheel was so proud.

title: The Banjo Who Felt Too Twangy
story:
In the Instrument Song Room, Robo could play every instrument. Piano, drums, rock guitar, harp and robot synth. But the banjo always sat in the back, quiet and shy. "My sound is too twangy," it told Robo. "Everyone likes the smooth piano better."

Robo picked up the banjo and gave it a strum. Plink-a-plink-a-twang! It was bouncy and bright, like a happy frog jumping across a pond. "I love your sound," said Robo. "Let's try it with the band."

He pressed BAND MODE. The drums began, the piano joined in, and then the banjo played its twangiest twang. Something wonderful happened. The whole song started to bounce! Everyone in the room tapped their feet.

From then on, the banjo sat right up front. Every time Robo pressed BAND MODE, it gave a proud little twang to say hello.

title: DJ Robo's Backwards Day
story:
In The Remix Room, DJ Robo spun songs in every style. Disco! Techno! Jazz! Chipmunk! Everyone danced while he hit the big DROP button.

But one morning, Robo pressed the backwards remix by accident. Suddenly, everything went backwards. People walked backwards into the room. King Gloop said "olleH" instead of "Hello." Even the disco ball spun the wrong way! "Oops," said Robo. "Or should I say, spoo!"

He tried to press the button again, but his hand went backwards too. Robo had to think. Then he turned all the way around, so his back faced the turntable. Now backwards was forwards! He pressed the button perfectly.

Everything went back to normal with a happy scratch sound. Everyone cheered. And King Gloop decided that saying olleH was actually pretty fun, so he kept doing it, just for laughs.

title: Robo's Wobbly Stage
story:
Robo was dancing on stage at Robo Rhythm. Left arrow, right arrow, up, down! The crowd cheered. But right in the middle of a song, the stage started to wobble.

Creak! One of the stage legs was loose. Every time Robo stepped, it tipped a little more.

Robo didn't want to stop the show. So he tried a new idea. He made his dance moves match the wobble. Tip left, step left. Tip right, step right. It looked like a brand-new dance! The crowd loved it. They started tipping and stepping too.

When the song ended, Robo took a bow and then quickly fixed the leg with a big screwdriver. Tighty-tight! The stage was safe again. But everyone kept asking for the wobble dance, so Robo added it to the show, even with the stage perfectly fixed.

title: The Coin That Ran Away
story:
Robo was running through Candy Land, grabbing coins as fast as he could. Ding, ding, ding! But one golden coin kept rolling away from him. Every time he reached for it, it zipped further ahead.

"Wait up!" Robo called. The coin rolled through Goo Jungle, past Space Station and onto Rainbow Road. Robo dashed, slid and jumped after it.

Finally, at the end of Rainbow Road, the coin stopped. It rolled in a little circle and said, "I'm sorry! I just wanted someone to race with. All the other coins sit still." Robo laughed, out of breath. "You're the fastest coin I've ever met!"

So instead of putting it in his pocket, Robo made the coin his running buddy. Now, every time Robo runs, a little golden coin rolls right beside him, and they race to the finish together.

title: The Kraken King's Tickle Spot
story:
Robo's little yellow submarine dove down, down, down into the deepest ocean zone. That's where the giant Kraken King lived. He loved playing tentacle tag, but today he wasn't playing. He was grumpy. "Something is stuck on my tentacle," he grumbled. "And I can't reach it!"

Robo shone his light. A shiny treasure chest was tangled in a long piece of seaweed, wrapped around the Kraken's arm. Robo carefully steered his submarine closer and used the little grabber claw to untangle it.

As he worked, the claw brushed the Kraken King's tentacle. "Hee hee hee!" The Kraken started to giggle. "That's my tickle spot!"

When the chest came free, the Kraken King was laughing so hard that bubbles filled the whole ocean. He let Robo keep the treasure. Then they played tentacle tag until it was time for bed.

title: The Case of the Borrowed Crown
story:
King Gloop's golden crown was missing! Detective Robo searched the Goo Castle. He found a little purple goo smudge in the throne room, another on the stairs, and a trail leading to the nursery.

He tiptoed in. There was Baby Gloop, wearing the crown, which was much too big. It slid down over Baby Gloop's eyes. "I just wanted to feel like a king," Baby Gloop whispered, peeking out from under it.

Robo didn't want Baby Gloop to feel bad. So instead of telling, he had an idea. He made a little paper crown, painted it gold, and put a shiny sticker on the front.

Then they walked back to the throne room together. Baby Gloop returned the big crown, and King Gloop smiled and placed the paper crown on his little one's head. "Now we're both kings!" The case was closed, with hugs.

title: Robo Gets Dizzy
story:
In Robo Pinball, Robo curled into a shiny pinball and bounced around the tables. Boing off King Gloop bumpers! Zoom through the candy machine! Whoosh through the secret wormhole!

He was having so much fun. But after a while, he started to feel a little dizzy. Round and round and round he went. "I need a break," Robo said, wobbling. But pinballs don't usually get breaks.

Then the flippers had an idea. Instead of flipping him, they held still and caught him, very gently, like a soft hand. Robo rolled into the little cozy spot between them and rested.

The King Gloop bumpers hummed a soft tune. The lights dimmed to a gentle glow. When Robo felt better, he gave the flippers a thumbs-up. Then flip! He was off again, bouncing and laughing, with a brand-new high score.

title: Sammy and the Campfire Marshmallow
story:
Sammy the cat had slipped out the door again! "Sweet freedom!" he meowed, dashing past the campfire into the dark backyard.

Ben grabbed his flashlight and his big net. He searched the bushes. He searched the garden. He even peeked inside the dark garage, where things went clink and clunk. No Sammy anywhere.

Then Ben had a clever idea. He went back to the campfire and toasted a marshmallow until it was golden and gooey. He didn't give it to Sammy, of course. Marshmallows are for people. But he sat very still and quiet, holding out a little bowl of Sammy's favorite treats.

A few moments later, two brown eyes peeked out from the woodpile. Sammy tiptoed over, sniffed, and started munching. Ben scooped him up for a cuddle. Sammy purred, all done adventuring for one night.

title: The Page That Wanted to Be Colored
story:
In The Coloring Room, there were eighteen coloring pages. Most of them were already bright and colorful. But one page was still just black lines on white. It showed Baby Gloop sneaking off with the crown. "Nobody has colored me yet," it sighed.

That night, the crayons rolled out of their box. "Let's surprise it!" said Purple. They each took a turn. Purple colored Baby Gloop. Gold colored the shiny crown. Green colored the grass, and Blue made a sky full of swirls.

Pink even added a little heart, just for fun.

In the morning, the page woke up and gasped. It was the most colorful page in the whole room! Ben printed it out and hung it on the fridge, right in the middle, where everybody could see it.

title: Robo's Twisty Maze
story:
In The Activity Room, Robo had made a brand-new maze. It had twisty paths and dead ends and a treasure in the middle. He was very proud of it.

But when he tried to solve it himself, he got lost! "Oh no," he laughed. "I made it too twisty!" He went left. Dead end. He went right. Another dead end. He tried the middle. Around and around.

Then he remembered a clever trick. He put his finger on the right-hand wall and kept it there, never letting go. He followed the wall around every corner and turn. Left, right, up, down.

And finally, there it was. The treasure in the middle! It was a gold star sticker. Robo stuck it right on his visor and smiled. Then he drew another maze, a little less twisty this time, so his friends could solve it too.

title: The Card at the Bottom of the Pack
story:
In Trading Cards, there were 144 Game Factory heroes and bosses. Every card wanted to be in the shiny binder. But one card always ended up at the very bottom of the pack. It was a little blue slime with a small smile.

"Nobody ever picks me," it said. One day, the computer challenged Ben to a battle. The computer had big, strong bosses. Ben's cards kept losing. Then Ben pulled the little blue slime out of the pack.

He read its card. It said: SPECIAL POWER: Makes everyone else slip and slide! Ben played it. All the computer's big bosses slipped on the slime and fell over in a heap. Ben won!

The little blue slime got the most special spot in the binder, the very first page. And it smiled a little bigger after that.

title: The Story That Had No Ending
story:
In Story Maker, Ben had picked a hero, a place, a bad guy, a magic item and something silly. The machine began to write. Once upon a time, a brave cat sailed to Pickle Island with a magic spoon...

But halfway through, the machine stopped. "Uh oh," it said. "I don't know how this story ends!" The brave cat looked around. The bad guy, a grumpy seagull, looked around too. "What happens now?" they asked.

Ben thought for a moment. Then he pressed a button and said, "The cat uses the magic spoon to make soup for everyone. Even the seagull."

The machine whirred happily. The cat stirred. The seagull smiled. Everyone on Pickle Island ate soup and danced. The machine printed the book and put it on the shelf. On the very last page, it said: The End, by Ben.

title: Sammy's Very Dramatic Bath
story:
It was bath day for Sammy, Ben's brown tabby cat. Sammy did not like bath day. He flopped on the floor. He meowed his loudest meow. He looked up with big, sad brown eyes.

"I know, I know," said Ben, gently. "But you rolled in the garden mud."

Sammy put one paw in the warm water and yanked it out. So dramatic! Ben thought about how to make it better. He got Sammy's softest towel and warmed it in the sun. He put on calm music. He used the tiniest cup to pour the water, very slowly.

Sammy grumbled, but he let it happen. When it was over, Ben wrapped him in the warm towel like a burrito. Sammy started to purr. Then Ben opened the back door. Sammy trotted outside, nice and clean, sniffed the air, and said, "Sweet freedom!"

title: The Printer Who Ran Out of Ink
story:
At The Print Shop, the big printer worked hard all day. It printed treasure hunts, award certificates, arcade tickets and puppet show tickets. Whirr, click, whoosh! But one afternoon, right in the middle of a certificate, it coughed. Pfft. The ink was gone! Half the certificate said Best Helper and the other half was blank.

"Oh no," said Robo. "Who was this certificate for?" They checked the order. It was for Jimmy the orange cat, for helping find a lost sock. Jimmy was waiting by the door, tapping his white paw, grumpy as usual.

Robo didn't want Jimmy to wait any longer. So he grabbed a box of crayons and finished the certificate by hand. He drew gold stars, a sock, and a big smiley face.

Jimmy looked at it for a long time. Then he purred. "This is better than printed." And he hung it right over his cat bed.

title: The Pillow Mountain
story:
In the Obstacle Course, Robo helped build a silly course around the house. There was a hallway crawl, a couch-cushion hop, a laundry-basket toss and, at the end, a giant pile of pillows called Pillow Mountain.

Ready, set, GO! The stopwatch started ticking. The racer crawled, hopped and tossed. But at Pillow Mountain, they got stuck. The pillows were too squishy to climb! "Hmm," said Robo. "Try going slow, like a bear."

So the racer crawled up very carefully, one pillow at a time. Squish, squish, squish. They reached the top and sat there, giggling. Then they slid all the way down the other side!

The stopwatch said it was the slowest time ever. But Robo cheered the loudest he had ever cheered. "That was the most fun anyone has ever had on Pillow Mountain!"

title: Robo Says Be Quiet
story:
Robo loved playing Robo Says. "Robo says hop like a frog! Robo says wiggle your nose! Touch your toes!" And everyone giggled when they touched their toes without him saying Robo says.

But one night, Robo's voice was tired. It came out tiny and squeaky. "Robo says... spin around," he croaked. Nobody could hear him! The family looked at each other. How could they play now?

Then Ben had an idea. "What if Robo does the moves, and we copy without words?" Robo loved it. He held up a card that said ROBO SAYS, then flapped his arms like a bird. Everyone flapped. He held up no card and patted his head. Two people patted their heads by mistake, and everybody laughed.

They played the quiet way until bedtime. Then Robo whispered, "Robo says, goodnight." And everyone whispered it back.

title: The Plane That Flew Backwards
story:
In Paper Airplanes, there were six cool planes to fold. The Dart flew straight. The Glider floated slowly. The Stunt Plane did loop-the-loops.

But one plane was folded a little bit wrong. When it was thrown at King Gloop's target, it zoomed forward, stopped in the air and then flew backwards! It landed right back in the thrower's hand. Everyone laughed. "That plane is broken!" said Robo.

King Gloop wobbled over and looked closely. "Broken? No, no! It's a BOOMERANG plane! It comes back to you!" They tried it again. Throw, swoop, catch! It was amazing. Soon everybody wanted to fold their plane a little bit wrong.

They named it the Gloop Boomerang, and it became plane number seven. King Gloop was so proud that he let it fly around his crown three times before he caught it.

title: The Painting Who Wanted to Move
story:
In The Art Gallery, twelve beautiful Game Factory pictures hung on the walls. One showed Robo on Moon Base. Another showed Sammy napping in the sun. Another showed Sparks running through a field.

But the picture of Sparks felt stuck. "I'm a running dog," it said. "But I can't move at all!" The other pictures wanted to help. Robo's picture had an idea. "When people look at you, they imagine you running. That's how you move."

That afternoon, Ben came to the gallery. He stopped in front of Sparks's picture for a long time. "I bet Sparks is running so fast," he said. "I bet he's chasing a butterfly, and Charlie and August are laughing inside."

The picture of Sparks felt a happy wiggle. It wasn't really moving. But in Ben's imagination, it was zooming everywhere.

title: The Bookmark That Got Lost in a Book
story:
In The Craft Room, everybody made something. Robo made a mask. King Gloop made a door hanger that said Gloop Zone. And a little striped bookmark was made for a big bedtime book.

That night, the bookmark marked the page perfectly. But the next morning, it was gone! It had slipped deep inside the book. The bookmark wandered between the pages. It saw dragons, pirates and a talking teapot. It was fun, but it wanted to go home.

Then it had a clever idea. It wiggled to the very top of a page and poked its tassel out, just a little bit, like a flag waving hello.

At bedtime, Ben opened the book and spotted the tassel. "There you are!" The bookmark slid right back to its place. It had loved its adventure, but it loved being home even more.

title: The Request Line Rings at Midnight
story:
DJ Robo was finishing his show on Robo Radio. He'd played game songs, told jokes and read the Game Factory news. Now it was almost midnight, and it was time to sign off.

Then the request line rang. Ring-ring! "Hello, Robo Radio!" Robo said. "Hi," came a tiny voice. It was Baby Gloop. "I can't sleep. Can you play a song?"

Robo looked at his songs. They were all very bouncy. Not good for sleeping. So he switched to 95.CHILL, slowed everything down and played the Moon Base song as soft as a whisper.

Then he talked quietly over the music. "Goodnight, Baby Gloop. Goodnight, moon. Goodnight, every game in the book." On the other end of the line, there was a tiny snore. Robo smiled, turned down the lights in the studio, and whispered, "This has been Robo Radio. Sweet dreams."

title: The Pancake Flip Disaster
story:
In The Cookbook, Robo and a grown-up chef were making pancakes. They mixed the flour, the milk and the eggs. They poured the batter into the warm pan. Sizzle! "Now," said Robo, "the big flip!"

He flipped the pancake way too high. It flew up, up, up and stuck to the ceiling! Everyone stared. Then they started laughing. The pancake slowly peeled off and plopped right on King Gloop's head. It sat there like a floppy hat.

"I've always wanted a pancake crown," said King Gloop proudly. Robo laughed so hard he had to sit down. Then he tried again, with a smaller, gentler flip this time. Flip, plop, perfect!

They made a whole stack. And when the chef printed the recipe card, they added a new tip at the bottom: Flip gently. Unless you want a pancake hat.

title: The Wobbly Pin Who Never Fell
story:
In Gloop Bowling, Robo rolled a shiny goo ball at ten wobbly Gloop pins. Wobble, wobble, BONK! Most of them tipped over and giggled.

But one little Gloop pin never fell. Every time the ball hit it, it wobbled way to the left, then way to the right, then bounced back up.

"How do you do that?" asked Robo. "I'm extra squishy," the pin said proudly. "I always bounce back!" The other pins were a bit jealous. So the squishy pin taught them how. "Don't be stiff," it said. "Just wobble with it, and let yourself bounce."

The next time Robo rolled, the ball hit the pins and they all wobbled, wobbled, wobbled... and stood right back up! Robo laughed. "No strikes today!" But nobody minded. The Gloop pins had a wobble party, and King Gloop joined in from the bonus round.

title: The Missing Jigsaw Piece
story:
In Jigsaw Puzzles, Ben was putting together a picture of Robo on Moon Base. It had ninety-six pieces. He worked and worked until only one spot was left. But where was the last piece?

He looked under the table. Not there. He looked in the box. Not there. He even looked behind the couch, where he found a sock and a crayon, but no puzzle piece.

Then he heard a little purr. Sammy the cat was lying on the rug, looking very cozy. Ben gently lifted one of Sammy's paws. There it was! The last puzzle piece, stuck to his fluffy fur.

"Sammy!" Ben laughed. "You were keeping it warm!" He snapped the last piece into place. The picture was complete. And Sammy, as a thank you for finding it, got to nap right on top of the finished puzzle.

title: The Pixel That Was Out of Place
story:
In the Pixel Art Studio, every picture was made of little squares called pixels. Ben was drawing Robo, one square at a time. White for his head, dark for his visor, blue for his eyes.

But when he finished, one pixel was orange! It was right on Robo's antenna. "Oops," said Ben. He reached to fix it. "Wait!" squeaked the orange pixel. "Please let me stay. I've always wanted to be in a picture of Robo."

Ben thought about it. He looked at the orange square. Then he smiled. "I know! You can be a little light on the tip of his antenna. Like a tiny beacon."

The orange pixel glowed with joy. Ben printed the picture as a cross-stitch, and the orange stitch looked just like a light. Now every time anyone looked at it, the little pixel shone proudly at the very top.

title: The Seed That Took Its Time
story:
In Robo's Garden, Ben planted five little seeds. Every day, Robo checked on them. "Grow, grow, grow!" he cheered.

By the end of the week, four seeds had sprouted. Tiny green leaves poked out of the dirt. But the fifth seed didn't do anything. The dirt stayed flat and brown.

"Maybe it's sad," said Robo. "Or maybe it's sleepy." So every morning, Robo gave the fifth seed a little water and sang it a song. He told it about the sunshine and the bumblebees. He said, "Take all the time you need."

Then one day, a little green sprout popped up, curly and strong. It grew, and grew, and grew, until it was taller than all the others. Taller than a crayon. Taller than a ruler. It was a sunflower! And its big yellow face turned to smile at Robo every morning.

title: The Goo That Wouldn't Stay Put
story:
In Robo's Science Lab, Robo and a grown-up made a batch of goo. They mixed and stirred until it was perfect. It was stretchy, slimy and bright green. "Now," said Robo, "let's guess. What will happen if we put it on a plate?"

They put it on a plate. And the goo slowly oozed right off the edge! Drip... drip... plop! It landed on the table. They put it back. It oozed off again. "It's escaping!" Robo laughed.

So Robo made a guess in his Lab Notebook. "Maybe goo likes to spread out." They tried a bowl instead of a plate. The goo oozed down the sides and settled at the bottom, nice and cozy.

"It worked!" cheered Robo. He wrote it in his notebook with a big star. And then they named the goo. It was called Oozy, and it lived in a happy little jar.

title: Rookie Robo's First Badge
story:
On the Super Chore Chart, Robo was just a Rookie. He wanted to level up all the way to Game Factory Legend. But first he needed his very first badge.

The mission was: Clean up your toys. Easy, thought Robo. But when he looked at the playroom, there were blocks, cars, crayons and a hundred tiny goo figures everywhere! "This will take forever," Robo groaned.

Then he had a clever idea. He made it a game! He set a timer for five minutes and pretended each toy was a lost bot buddy that needed rescuing. Blocks to the block box. Cars to the car garage. Goo figures back home.

Beep beep beep! When the timer went off, the room was spotless. Robo earned his very first badge, a shiny star that said Toy Rescuer. He stuck it right on his chest and danced around the clean room.

title: The Clue That Led to a Friend
story:
In the Scavenger Hunt, Robo had a list of clues. Find something round like a Gloop bumper. Find something soft like Sammy's fur. Find something shiny like Robo's visor.

Ben ran around the house, checking things off. A ball for round. A pillow for soft. A spoon for shiny! There was just one clue left. It said: Find something that makes you happy.

Ben looked everywhere. His toys made him happy. His games made him happy. But which one was the answer? Then Sammy the cat walked into the room and rubbed against Ben's leg. He purred loudly and flopped over for a belly rub.

Ben laughed. "Found it!" He checked off the last clue with a big smile. Robo cheered. Sammy got a cuddle. And the scavenger hunt ended with everybody happy, which was the best prize of all.

title: The Fort That Fell Down
story:
In Fort Builder, Robo made a blueprint for the best pillow fort ever. It had a tunnel, a lookout tower and a secret room. Ben built it, pillow by pillow, blanket by blanket.

It was perfect. Until it fell down! Floomp! Pillows everywhere. Ben sat in the middle of the pile, a little sad. Robo patted his shoulder. "Every great builder has a fort fall down sometimes. Let's figure out why."

They looked carefully. The tall tower had been too wobbly. So this time, they used the big couch cushions at the bottom and the little pillows on top. They used chairs to hold up the blanket roof. They clipped the corners with clothespins.

The new fort was even better than the first one. They hung a flag on top and made a secret password: Gloop Gloop Goo. And it stayed up all night long.

title: The Island With No Name
story:
In World Map Maker, Ben drew a brand-new Game Factory world. There was a candy island, a volcano island, a castle island and a spooky island. He drew a dotted path between all of them.

But off in the corner, there was one tiny island that he had forgotten to name. It had just one palm tree and a little sandy beach.

"What do I do on this island?" Ben wondered. It didn't have a boss or a castle. Robo looked at the map. "Maybe it's a resting island," he said. "After you beat all the bosses, you can come here and relax."

Ben loved that idea. He drew a hammock between two trees, a lemonade stand and a little sign. It said Rest Island: No Bosses Allowed. It became everyone's favorite spot on the whole map, and the dotted path ended right there.

title: A Card for King Gloop
story:
In Game Factory Cards, everybody was making greeting cards. Robo made one for Sparks. Sammy made one for Ben. Duke Googool made a very fancy one for himself. But King Gloop looked around and noticed something. Nobody was making a card for Baby Gloop.

"Hmm," King Gloop said. He picked out the brightest purple paper. He drew a big wobbly heart and a little crown on top. Inside, he wrote: To my favorite little goo. You make our castle wobble with joy.

He folded it carefully and left it on Baby Gloop's pillow. That night, Baby Gloop found the card and read it three times. Then Baby Gloop made a card too. It said: To the best dad goo in the galaxy.

The next morning, both cards were hanging on the castle wall, side by side, right where everyone could see them.

title: The Slowest Race Wins
story:
At Games Day, Robo ran the show. There was a sack race, an egg-and-spoon race and a silly backwards walk. Every event had medals and a podium ceremony. Then Robo announced the last event. "The Slow Motion Race!"

Everybody looked confused. "Slow?" "Yes!" said Robo. "Whoever crosses the finish line LAST wins!" The racers took tiny steps. Then tinier steps. Then they wobbled like jelly, trying not to fall over. One person walked so slowly that a ladybug passed them!

Everyone laughed so hard their tummies hurt. The judges held up big scorecards, and the last person to cross the line got the gold medal.

At the podium ceremony, Robo played the victory song extra slowly, just to match. And all the winners and racers bowed together, very, very, very slowly.

title: Agent Whiskers and the Secret Snack
story:
At Spy Academy, Agent Nega and Agent Whiskers had a new mission. Someone had hidden the secret snack, and they had to find it using only clues.

Agent Nega spun the decoder wheel. The first clue said: Look where things stay cold. They checked the fridge. Inside was another clue: Look where things get clean. They checked the bathtub. Another clue! Look where Agent Whiskers sleeps.

Agent Whiskers tilted his head and adjusted his spy collar. He trotted to his favorite cozy basket and sniffed. There, tucked under the blanket, was a little box with a ribbon.

Inside were crunchy cat treats for Agent Whiskers and a shiny battery snack for Agent Nega. Nega-Robo's red visor glowed with joy. "Mission complete," said Agent Nega. Agent Whiskers purred, munched his treat and promptly fell asleep. Even spies need naps.

title: Jimmy's Hidden Talent
story:
At the Game Factory Talent Show, DJ Robo was the host. Robo juggled. King Gloop sang. Sammy did a very dramatic flop. The judges held up big scores.

Then it was Jimmy's turn. Jimmy, the grumpy orange cat with the white paws, sat on the stage and didn't move. "Come on, Jimmy," whispered Robo. "Show us your talent!" Jimmy flicked his tail. "I don't have one," he grumbled.

But then the stage lights warmed up, and a sunbeam landed right next to Jimmy. He couldn't help it. He stretched out, rolled over, and curled into the most perfect, round, cozy ball anyone had ever seen.

The audience went "Awwww!" The judges held up their cards: ten, ten, ten! Jimmy won the award for Best Napper in the Whole Factory. He pretended not to care. But his green eyes were sparkling.

title: The Speech Bubble Mix-Up
story:
In the Comic Book Maker, Ben was making a comic about Robo. In the first box, Robo flew through space. In the second box, King Gloop waved hello. In the third box, Sammy took a nap.

But when Ben added the speech bubbles, they got mixed up! Now Robo said "Meow." Sammy said "BOOM!" And King Gloop said "Beep boop, I am a robot."

Ben started to fix them. But then he read the page again, and he laughed so hard he snorted. "Wait," he said. "This is funnier!" So he kept it. He even added more. A tree said "Hello, I am a cupcake." The moon said "Sweet freedom!"

When Ben printed the comic, everyone who read it laughed out loud. It was called The Day Everyone Said the Wrong Thing, and it was the funniest comic in the whole Game Factory.

title: The Goo Slide That Went Up
story:
In Board Game Maker, Ben designed a brand-new board game. There were jet tubes that zoomed you forward, goo slides that slid you back and mystery cards with surprises.

The family played it together. Everyone was having fun. But one grown-up landed on a goo slide every single turn! He slid back, and back, and back again. "Oh no," said the grown-up, pretending to cry. "I'll never win!"

Ben looked at the board. Then he had a kind idea. He grabbed a pencil and drew one new space right in the middle. He called it the Upside-Down Goo Slide. If you landed on it, you slid UP instead of down!

On the very next turn, the grown-up landed right on it. Whoosh! All the way up near the finish line. Everybody cheered. Nobody knew who would win now. And that made it the best game ever.

title: The Gloop Buck That Was Too Small
story:
In the Game Factory Shop, Ben was the shopkeeper. Customers came in to buy toys, and they paid with Gloop Bucks. Ding! went the cash register.

Then Baby Gloop came in, holding one tiny Gloop Buck very tightly. Baby Gloop pointed at a big stuffed Robo toy on the shelf. It cost five Gloop Bucks.

Baby Gloop looked at the one little coin. Then at the toy. Then back at the coin. Its wobbly lip started to shake. Ben thought hard. Then he smiled. "Actually, today is a special sale day! Anyone who comes in with a big smile gets four extra Gloop Bucks!"

Baby Gloop gave the biggest smile ever. Ben counted out four more bucks, and together they paid for the toy. Ding! Baby Gloop hugged the stuffed Robo all the way home. And Ben put up a sign: Smile Sale Every Day.

title: Robo Predicts a Rainbow
story:
It was time for the Weather Reporter show. Ben looked outside. It was raining! Drip, drop, drip. "Good morning, everyone," said Ben on air. "Today's weather is... rainy."

Robo sighed. "Rainy days are a little gloomy." But Ben kept looking out the window. The clouds were moving. A tiny bit of sunshine was peeking through the edge. And Ben remembered something he had learned.

"Wait!" he said into the microphone. "When there's rain AND sunshine at the same time, you know what you get?" Robo's blue eyes went wide. "A rainbow?"

They both ran to the window. And there it was, a giant rainbow stretching right across the sky! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. "Breaking news!" said Ben. "Today's weather is rainbow!" And Robo danced all the way through the weather report.

title: The Sticker That Wouldn't Stick
story:
In Sticker Maker, Ben designed a whole sheet of stickers. There was a holo Robo, a sparkly King Gloop, a Sammy with a big smile and a Duke Googool with extra-shiny top hat.

They peeled off and stuck to notebooks, lunchboxes and the fridge. But one Sammy sticker just wouldn't stick. It kept falling off and landing on the floor. "Why can't I stick?" it said sadly.

Ben picked it up and looked at it. The back was a little dusty. He blew on it gently. Phoo! Then he thought about where Sammy the real cat liked to be. "I know the perfect spot!"

He stuck the sticker on Sammy's food bowl. This time it stuck perfectly! Now every morning, when the real Sammy ate breakfast, the sticker Sammy smiled up at him. And they both looked very happy about it.

title: Nega-Robo's Easiest Puzzle
story:
In the Home Escape Room, Nega-Robo had hidden clue cards all over the house. The family had to solve each puzzle before the timer ran out.

They found the first clue under a pillow. They found the second one taped to the bathroom mirror. The third one was inside a boot! Every puzzle was tricky, but they solved them together.

Then they got to the very last lock. The clue said: The answer is the thing that makes every puzzle easier. "Hmm," said Ben. "A flashlight? A pencil? A magnifying glass?" They tried them all. None of them worked. Time was running out!

Then Ben looked around at his family, all crowded close, helping. "Oh! It's teamwork!" They typed it in. Click! The lock opened. Inside was a note from Nega-Robo that said: Correct. Great job, team. His red visor was drawn smiling.

title: The Statue Under the Sheet
story:
In The Boss Museum, there were statues of sixty bosses. Robo was the tour guide. He told everyone about each one. When a player beat a boss, its statue turned shiny gold.

But in the corner, there was one statue still covered by a big white sheet. "What's under there?" everyone asked.

"That's a secret," said Robo, with a wink. One night, after the museum closed, Robo heard a tiny sneeze from under the sheet. Achoo! He tiptoed over. "Are you okay?" "The sheet is dusty," said a small voice. "And I'm a little lonely in here."

Robo thought about it. He couldn't take off the sheet. That would spoil the surprise. But he could keep the statue company. So he sat down beside it and told it all the stories of the other bosses until it fell asleep. And he brought a feather duster the next day.

title: The Door That Opened Too Early
story:
On the Countdown Calendar, every day had a little door. Behind each door was a surprise. Robo was in charge of making sure each door opened on the right day.

But one morning, Robo found a door already open. It was for a day that was still a whole week away! "Uh oh," said Robo. "Who opened it?"

He looked closer. Inside the door was a tiny bluebird, sitting in a nest made from paper confetti. "Sorry," it chirped. "It looked so cozy in here, I just moved in." Robo didn't want to make the bluebird leave. But the surprise was supposed to be there on its day!

So Robo had an idea. He helped the bluebird build a brand-new nest on top of the calendar, right where it could watch every door open. And when that special day came, the surprise behind the door was a bluebird song.

title: Sammy and the Golden Gloop Fish
story:
Sammy the tabby cat rowed his little boat to his favorite fishing spot. He had caught forty fishy things for his Fish Album, and some junk too, like an old boot and a rubber duck. There was only one left: the Golden Gloop Fish.

Sammy waited. And waited. His brown eyes watched the water. Then, sparkle! The Golden Gloop Fish swam right up to his boat.

But it looked worried. "Please don't put me in a bucket," it said. "I like swimming free." Sammy understood. He loved freedom too. So he took out his album and his crayons instead. "Can I draw you, then?"

The fish posed proudly, fins sparkling. Sammy drew the most beautiful picture of it. Then he waved goodbye as it swam away. He rowed home with a full album and a happy heart. "Sweet freedom," he purred, "for everyone."

title: The Box That Giggled
story:
Deep in the Game Factory, there was a little box with a big question mark painted on top. Nobody knew what was inside. Not Robo. Not King Gloop. Not even Duke Googool, who usually knew everything.

One day, the box giggled. "Hee hee hee!" Everyone gathered around. "Did that box just laugh?" whispered Baby Gloop. Robo leaned in close. "Hello, little box. What's inside you?"

"That's a secret!" said the box. "It's a surprise. And surprises are best when you wait just a little bit." So they waited. They guessed and guessed. Was it something sparkly? Something silly? Something with polka dots? Every guess made the box giggle more.

Finally, Robo said, "We'll find out when the time is right." And the box hummed happily, keeping its secret safe, while everyone smiled, excited about what was coming.

title: The Party With No Theme
story:
In the Party Planner, Robo helped plan the biggest Game Factory party ever. But there was a problem. Everyone wanted a different theme! King Gloop wanted a goo party. Sparks wanted a dog party. Duke Googool wanted a fancy tea party. And Sammy just wanted a nap party.

"Oh dear," said Robo. "We can only pick one." Everyone started to argue. Then Robo had a clever idea. "What if each room has a different theme?"

So the kitchen was goo, with green jelly and wobbly cups. The living room was full of dog toys. The dining room had teacups and little sandwiches. And the bedroom had blankets, pillows and quiet music for napping.

Everybody wandered from room to room all evening. And at the end, they all ended up in the nap room, cozy and full, with Sammy right in the middle, purring the loudest.

title: The Arcade That Ran Out of Coins
story:
Ben built his very own paper arcade machine. It had a cool skin with stars and lightning bolts. He slid in a game screen card and made arcade coins out of paper. Everyone in the family lined up to play. Insert coin, ding! Play! Then high score! But soon the paper coins were all used up.

"Oh no," said Ben. "No more coins!" Robo looked at the empty coin box. "What if we earn coins instead? You could do a silly dance for one coin. Or tell a joke for two coins."

Everyone loved it. A grown-up did a silly dance. Ben told a joke about King Gloop and got two coins. Even Sammy the cat earned a coin, just by sitting on the arcade machine and looking cute.

By the end of the night, everyone had played, laughed and danced. The arcade machine had the best high score sheet ever.

title: The Sock Who Missed Every Time
story:
At Toss Targets, giant paper targets were taped to the wall. Everyone tossed rolled-up socks at them. Thwump! Bullseye! The Scorekeeper shot out confetti.

But one striped sock always missed. It flew too far left. Then too far right. Once it landed in the laundry basket! "I'm the worst sock ever," it sighed.

Robo picked it up and looked closely. "Aha! You're not rolled up tight enough. You're all floppy." He helped the sock roll into a nice, snug ball. The next toss, it flew straight and true. Thwump! Right in the middle! The confetti went everywhere.

The striped sock was so happy. It got a gold star on the scorecard. And after that, whenever another sock felt floppy, the striped sock showed it how to roll up nice and tight.

title: The Paper That Kept a Secret
story:
In the Game Factory, there was a stack of paper with a big question mark on top. It was waiting to become something. But nobody knew what! Robo tapped the paper. "What are you going to be?"

The paper rustled. "It's a surprise!" King Gloop guessed it would be a crown. Sammy guessed it would be a cozy bed. Duke Googool guessed it would be a very fancy hat. The paper just wiggled happily and didn't say a word.

All day long, everyone tried to peek. They tried looking from the side. They tried looking from underneath. Baby Gloop even tried tickling it!

But the paper kept its secret. "Good surprises are worth waiting for," it said. That night, everyone went to bed wondering and smiling. Because the best part of a surprise is all the fun of guessing.

title: The Town That Needed a Park
story:
Ben built a whole Paper Game Factory Town. There were tall buildings, little houses, roads, cars and paper heroes walking everywhere. Robo stood on the corner waving at everyone.

But after a while, the paper heroes looked tired. "There's nowhere to play," said a paper Sammy. "It's all buildings and roads." Ben looked at his town map. They were right! He had forgotten a park.
