So he got busy. He cut out green paper for grass. He folded paper trees, a paper swing set and a little paper pond. He even made a paper bench for Duke Googool to sit on and drink his tea.

He put the park right in the middle of town. The paper heroes cheered. Robo zoomed down the paper slide. Sammy lay in the paper sunshine. And the town felt like a real home at last.

title: The Cube Buddy With a Round Head
story:
In Cube Buddies, everyone had a cube head. Robo had a cube head. King Gloop had a cube head. Even Sparks had a long cube head. They all stood on the display stage, spinning in 3D.

Then Ben designed a brand-new buddy. But when he folded it, the head came out a little bit round on top. Oops! The new buddy looked at all the square heads. "I'm different," it said quietly.

The other Cube Buddies spun around to look. Then Robo said, "You know what? You're the only one who can roll!" The new buddy tried it. Roll, roll, roll! It rolled across the whole stage and back again. The others clapped their little paper hands.

From then on, the round-headed buddy had the most important job of all. It rolled up and down the stage, saying good morning to every Cube Buddy, every single day.

title: The Prize That Nobody Won
story:
At the Game Factory Carnival, there were eight booths. The ring toss, the cup stack, the sock bucket and more. Everyone played and won tickets. Then they traded their tickets at PRIZE TIME.

But one prize sat on the shelf all day. It was a big, fluffy teddy bear. It cost the most tickets, and nobody had enough. The bear looked sad as the carnival ended. "Nobody wants me," it thought.

Then Robo had an idea. "What if everyone puts their leftover tickets together?" Ben gave three. Sammy gave one he'd found under the couch. King Gloop gave seven. Everyone added a few. They counted. It was exactly enough!

But who would get the bear? They decided it would belong to everyone. It sat on the big couch, where anyone could hug it. And it was the happiest teddy bear in the whole Game Factory.

title: The Crown That Went on Vacation
story:
King Gloop woke up one morning and his crown was gone! He called the whole family together. "A real mystery!" he gasped.

They hunted for printed clues around the house. One clue was under a pillow. One was taped behind a door. One was hidden in a shoe. Each clue had a secret code to crack. The codes spelled out: SUNNY. WARM. WINDOW.

Everybody ran to the sunniest window in the house. And there, sitting on the windowsill, was the golden crown, shining in the sun. Next to it was a little note in wobbly writing. It said: I was a bit cold. I went to warm up. Love, the Crown.

King Gloop laughed so hard he jiggled. "My crown took a vacation!" He put it back on his head. It was warm and toasty, and it felt wonderful. Case closed!

title: The Magic Mirror's Favorite Costume
story:
In the Dress Up Kit, everyone made costumes. Robo visors, King Gloop crowns, Duke Googool's tall top hat and even a Sammy tail. Then they stood in front of the Magic Mirror to see how they looked.

"Ooh, fancy!" said the Magic Mirror to the top hat. "How royal!" it said to the crown. But then Ben came up, wearing everything all at once. A visor, a crown, a top hat stacked on top, and a tail. He looked very silly.

The Magic Mirror was quiet for a moment. Then it burst out laughing. "That's my favorite one of all!" Ben laughed too. Everybody started mixing their costumes. Robo wore the tail. King Gloop wore the visor. Duke Googool wore two top hats.

Then they all walked in the Costume Parade, the silliest parade ever, and the Magic Mirror cheered for every single one.

title: Countdown for a Tiny Pilot
story:
In Straw Rocket Launch, eleven rockets stood ready on the launch pad. Each one had a pilot. Robo, King Gloop, Sammy and more. Everyone took turns blowing into their straws and launching them high!

But one tiny pilot, a little bot buddy, was nervous. "What if I fly too high? What if I never come back down?" Robo sat next to the little rocket. "You know what? I get nervous too, before every launch. Let's count down together."

They held hands. "Five, four, three, two, one..." Whoosh! The little rocket flew up, up, up. It did a loop in the air. It saw the whole room from up high. Then it floated gently down and landed on a soft pillow.

"I did it!" cheered the tiny pilot. "Can I go again?" And the little bot buddy launched all afternoon, laughing every time.

title: Sammy's Quietest Tiptoe
story:
Sammy the cat wanted to get to the back door. Sweet freedom was waiting outside! But he had to sneak through eight rooms without getting caught.

He tiptoed past the kitchen. He crept under the couch. He hid behind a plant. So far, so good! Then, in the hallway, he found a squeaky toy right in his path. If he stepped on it, everyone would hear. Squeak!

Sammy thought hard. He couldn't jump over it. He couldn't go around. Then he had a clever idea. He picked the toy up very gently in his mouth, carried it to his bed and tucked it under his blanket, nice and quiet.

Then he tiptoed the rest of the way to the door. Just as he got there, Ben opened it. "Hi Sammy! Want to go outside?" Sammy blinked his brown eyes and trotted out into the sunshine. "Sweet freedom!"

title: Puff's Little Fire
story:
In Dragon Sky Race, the dragons flew through glowing rings all the way to the Rainbow Castle. Sparkle was the fastest. Thunder was the strongest. And Puff was the littlest, with a tiny puff of smoke instead of fire.

Halfway through the race, a cold wind blew. Brrr! The glowing rings started to fade. Without them, nobody would know where to go! Sparkle tried to relight them with a big blast of fire, but it was too hot. The rings almost burned up. Thunder tried, but his fire was too strong.

Then Puff flew to the first ring and gave a tiny, gentle puff. The ring glowed warm and bright again. It was just right!

Puff flew from ring to ring, lighting every one. The other dragons followed. When they reached the Rainbow Castle, everybody cheered for Puff, the littlest dragon with the most perfect fire.

title: The Boss Who Wanted to Be Bonked
story:
In Boss Builder Battle, Ben built a brand-new boss. It had green goo, a spinning drill, a little laser and a crown on top. It stomped into the arena, ready for battle!

But when Robo arrived, the boss looked nervous. "Please be gentle," it said. "This is my very first battle."

Robo smiled. "Don't worry. Bonks don't hurt. They tickle!" The boss swung its drill. Robo jumped. The boss shot its laser. Robo dodged. Then Robo bounced right on top of its crown. Bonk! "Hee hee!" the boss giggled. "That does tickle!"

They battled until the boss was laughing too hard to fight. Then it flopped over and waved its goo hands. "You win!" After the battle, Robo and the boss shared a juice box. "Can we do it again tomorrow?" the boss asked. Robo grinned. "Every day if you want!"

title: The Rabbit Who Wouldn't Come Out
story:
At Robo's Magic Show, Robo wore a sparkly cape and a tall black hat. "For my next trick," he said, "I will pull a rabbit out of my hat!"

He waved his magic wand. He said the magic words. Abraca-robo! He reached into the hat. But there was no rabbit!

The audience gasped. Robo looked inside. There was a little rabbit, all curled up, peeking at him. "I'm shy," it whispered. "There are too many people." Robo had an idea. He turned to the audience. "Everyone, close your eyes and count to three very quietly."

They all closed their eyes. "One... two... three..." Robo gently lifted the rabbit out. When they opened their eyes, there it was, sitting on Robo's head and wiggling its nose! The crowd clapped softly. The rabbit felt brave. And Robo said it was the best trick of all.

title: The Big Boss Dog's Lost Ball
story:
Ninja Cat hopped across the night-time rooftops, collecting golden fish. Leap! Land! Tiptoe past a sleepy guard dog. So far, so good.

Then, on the very tallest rooftop, Ninja Cat heard a sad whine. It was the Big Boss Dog! He was big and gruff, but now he looked worried. "My favorite ball rolled into the gutter," he sniffled. "I can't reach it. My paws are too big."

Ninja Cat looked at the narrow gutter. Ninja Cat was small and quick, and flipped down, wiggled along the edge and grabbed the ball with her paws. Ninja Cat rolled it right back to him. The Big Boss Dog's tail started to wag. Thump, thump, thump!

"Thank you, little ninja," he said. "You can cross my rooftops any time." From then on, they played catch under the moon every night, and Ninja Cat always won.

title: The Present on the Doorstep
story:
One morning, Robo opened the door of Moon Base and found a big box on the doorstep. It was wrapped in shiny paper with a giant bow. On top, there was a tag with a question mark. "Who is it for?" asked Robo.

King Gloop wobbled over. "Maybe it's for me!" Baby Gloop bounced up. "Maybe it's for me!" Sammy the cat sniffed the bow and sat right on top of it. Robo looked at the tag again. On the back, in tiny letters, it said: For everyone. Open together.

So they all held hands around the box. They counted to three. One, two, three! But just as they were about to pull the bow, the box gave a happy little wiggle, as if to say, "Not yet!"

Everyone laughed. They decided to wait for the perfect moment. And the waiting was almost as fun as the surprise.

title: The Question Mark That Bounced
story:
In a quiet corner of the Game Factory book, a big purple question mark was bouncing all by itself. Boing! Boing! Boing!

Robo walked by and stopped. "Hello! Why are you bouncing?" "I'm too excited to sit still!" said the question mark. "I'm holding a surprise, and I can't tell anyone what it is!" Robo grinned. "Not even a tiny hint?"

The question mark bounced higher. "Nope! But I can tell you this: it's big, it's fun, and it's for the whole family." Robo started bouncing too. Then King Gloop, then Baby Gloop, then Sparks. Soon the whole page was full of bouncing friends, all giggling and guessing.

At bedtime, the question mark finally settled down. It yawned and curled into a little ball. "Goodnight, everyone," it said. "The surprise will still be here tomorrow."

title: The Treasure Map With No X
story:
One day, Robo found an old treasure map tucked inside the Game Factory book. It had dotted lines, swirly arrows and little drawings of trees and hills. But where the X should be, there was only a big question mark.

"How can we find the treasure without an X?" asked Duke Googool, adjusting his monocle. Robo studied the map. He followed the dotted line with his finger. It went past the kitchen, around the couch and back to the very start.

"Hmm," said Robo. "It goes in a circle." Then Baby Gloop said something very wise. "Maybe the treasure is going on the adventure together."

Everyone smiled. They folded up the map and put it in a safe spot. Whatever the real surprise was, they would find out someday. And until then, they had the most fun following circles.

title: The Envelope That Waited
story:
In the mailbox at Moon Base, there was a special envelope. It was golden, with a big red question mark sticker on the back. It said: Do not open until the right day.

Robo held it up to the light. He couldn't see a thing. He shook it gently. It didn't rattle. He sniffed it. It smelled a little like happiness. "When is the right day?" asked Sammy the cat.

"I don't know," said Robo. "But I bet we'll know when it comes." So Robo put the envelope on the shelf, right in the middle, where everyone could see it. Every morning, they said good morning to the envelope. Every night, they said goodnight.

The envelope seemed to glow a little bit brighter each day, as if it was getting more and more excited. And so was everybody else.

title: Robo's Guessing Game
story:
One rainy afternoon, Robo found a box wrapped in rainbow paper with a question mark on top. He called all his friends over. "Let's play a guessing game!"

King Gloop guessed first. "Is it a giant jelly?" The box shook gently, side to side. No! Sparks barked. "Is it a bone?" The box shook again. No!

Duke Googool guessed a teapot. Baby Gloop guessed a bouncy castle. Sammy guessed a sunbeam. Every time, the box shook no, and every time, everybody laughed harder. Finally, Robo asked, "Is it something we'll all love?" The box hopped up and down. YES!

That was all they needed to know. They put the box back on the shelf, gave it a little pat and went to make hot cocoa. Some surprises are perfect just the way they are, still waiting.

title: The Ribbon That Kept Growing
story:
On a big gift box in the Game Factory, there was a long red ribbon. Robo wanted to untie it. He pulled one end. The ribbon kept coming. And coming. And coming!

He pulled it across the room. Around the table. Up the stairs. King Gloop grabbed the other end and pulled too. Soon the whole house was wrapped in red ribbon, like a giant present!

"This box really loves surprises," laughed Robo. Then Sammy the cat came in and saw all that ribbon. His brown eyes went wide. He pounced! He tumbled! He got the ribbon wrapped around his tail.

Everyone was laughing so hard that they forgot all about opening the box. They spent the whole evening untangling Sammy. At the end, the box was still closed, sitting quietly with a fresh new bow. It seemed to be smiling.

title: The Huggy Gloop Zombie
story:
It was Zombie Tag Night! Everyone had flashlights. The lights were off, and the Gloop Zombies were shuffling through the house, arms out wide. "Brainsss," moaned one zombie. Then it stopped. "No, wait. Hugsss!"

That's right. These were huggy zombies. If they caught you, you got a big, squishy hug. Ben hid behind the couch. His flashlight beam wobbled. Then he heard a sad sound from the hallway. One little Gloop Zombie had bumped its toe and was sitting on the floor.

Ben forgot all about hiding. He came out and shone his flashlight on the little zombie's toe. "Are you okay?" The zombie sniffled. Then it smiled and said, "You found me! Do I get a hug?"

Ben gave it the biggest hug ever. Then they teamed up and went looking for everybody else, giggling all the way.

title: Robo's Bow Tie Problem
story:
It was almost time for The Game Factory Game Show. The lights were bright. The teams had their big buzzers. The crown, medal and trophy were waiting on a shiny table.

But Robo, the host, had a problem. His bow tie was crooked! He tried to fix it. Now it was upside down. He tried again. Now it was tied around his antenna! "Oh no," said Robo. "I can't host like this!"

The teams looked at each other. Then Sammy jumped up and gently batted the bow tie with his paw. It spun around. King Gloop straightened it with his goo hands. Baby Gloop gave it a little tug.

Ta-da! It was perfect. "Thank you, everyone," said Robo. "You all get bonus points for teamwork!" The audience cheered. Then he pressed the buzzer, and the show began, with the straightest bow tie ever.

title: The Dish Nobody Ordered
story:
At the Game Factory Restaurant, the menu was full of silly dishes. Goo noodles. Robo bolts with ketchup. Moon cheese pizza. Rocket fuel smoothie. The chef was busy cooking, and the timer sizzled.

"Order up!" called the chef, ringing the bell. But one dish on the menu had never been ordered. It was called Mystery Soup. Nobody knew what it was, so nobody tried it.

Then Jimmy the orange cat sat down at a table. He grumbled at the menu. "Everything here is too silly. I'll take the Mystery Soup." The chef stirred and stirred. Out came a warm bowl of... cozy chicken soup. Plain, simple and perfect.

Jimmy took a sip. His green eyes went soft. "This," he said, "is exactly what I wanted." He gave the restaurant five stars. And Mystery Soup became the special of the day, every day.

title: The Tiny Box Inside the Big Box
story:
Robo found a big box with a question mark on top. He opened it. Inside, there was a smaller box, also with a question mark! He opened that one. Inside was an even smaller box!

"How many boxes are there?" laughed King Gloop. Robo kept opening. Box, box, box. They got smaller and smaller. Baby Gloop had to hold them all. Sparks stacked them in a tall tower.

Finally, Robo got to the tiniest box of all. It was as small as a button. He opened it very carefully. Inside was a teeny piece of paper. It said: Almost there! Keep being curious!

Everyone burst out laughing. "It's a surprise about a surprise!" said Duke Googool. They put all the boxes back together, one inside the other, and set them on the shelf. Now they knew one thing for sure: something wonderful was coming.

title: The Night the Stars Spelled a Question
story:
One night on Moon Base, Robo looked up at the sky. The stars were twinkling in a funny shape. They made a giant question mark!

"Look!" said Robo. Everyone came running outside. King Gloop. Baby Gloop. Duke Googool with his teacup. Even Nega-Robo, his red visor glowing in the dark. "What does it mean?" asked Baby Gloop.

"I think," said Robo slowly, "the sky is telling us a surprise is coming." They lay down on a big blanket and watched. The question mark twinkled brighter. Then one star blinked three times, like a wink.

Everyone giggled. They made up stories about what the surprise might be, each one sillier than the last. A flying pancake! A dancing moon! A giant hug from the sky! They all fell asleep under the stars, dreaming happy, wondering dreams.

title: The Locked Treasure Chest
story:
In the middle of the Game Factory, there appeared a wooden treasure chest. It had golden corners and a big lock shaped like a question mark.

"I bet there's something amazing inside," said Robo. They tried to open it. Duke Googool tried his fancy key. No luck. King Gloop tried to squish it open. No luck. Sparks tried to sniff it open, which doesn't really work.

Then Robo noticed tiny letters on the lock. They said: Only opens with a smile. Everybody looked at each other. Then they smiled. Big, silly, toothy smiles! Baby Gloop smiled so wide its face wobbled.

The lock gave a happy click. The lid opened just a crack, and a warm golden glow came out. But then it closed again with a gentle thump, and a note slid out: Not today. But soon! Everyone cheered anyway. Soon was good enough.

title: The Surprise Balloon
story:
One morning, a big red balloon floated into the Game Factory. It had a question mark painted on it in gold. It bobbed gently above Robo's head.

"Hello, balloon," said Robo. "Where did you come from?" The balloon bobbed. It floated over to King Gloop and bounced on his crown. It floated to Sammy the cat, who batted it with a paw. Then it floated out the window!

"Follow it!" said Robo. They all ran outside. The balloon floated over the garden, past the swing and around the big tree. Everyone chased it, laughing and tripping and having the best time.

Finally, the balloon landed softly in Robo's hands. It had a little string with a tag. The tag said: Thanks for playing! The real surprise is coming soon. Everyone was out of breath and smiling. Robo tied the balloon to the door, where it bobbed happily all day.

title: The Whispering Gift
story:
At the end of a long day, Robo found a small gift on his pillow. It was wrapped in blue paper with silver question marks. When he picked it up, he heard a tiny voice. "Psst," it whispered. "Can you keep a secret?"

Robo nodded. "Good," said the gift. "Because I'm not ready to tell you what I am yet." Robo laughed softly. "Then why are you whispering?" "Because it's bedtime," said the gift. "And surprises need sleep too, so they can be extra exciting in the morning."

So Robo tucked the gift into a little blanket next to his pillow. He turned off the light. He could almost hear the gift humming a sleepy tune.

"Goodnight, little surprise," Robo whispered. "Goodnight, Robo," the gift whispered back. "Sweet dreams. I'll be here when it's time."

title: The Ghost Who Was Afraid of the Dark
story:
Ben turned the living room into a Game Factory Haunted House. There were ten spooky stations, paper tombstones and a sound board that went "Wooooo!" Everyone was having silly-spooky fun.

But at the last station, there was a little paper ghost sitting in the corner, shivering. "What's wrong?" asked Robo. "I'm scared of the dark," whispered the ghost. "Isn't that silly? A ghost who's scared of the dark!"

Robo didn't think it was silly at all. Lots of people are scared of the dark. He thought for a moment. Then he grabbed a little flashlight and gave it to the ghost. "Here. Now you can make your own light."

The ghost clicked it on. Its face lit up with a big smile. Then it zoomed around the haunted house, shining its flashlight and saying "Boo!" in the friendliest voice ever. It was the happiest haunted house in town.

title: The Rice Shaker Solo
story:
At the Game Factory Rock Concert, the family band was ready to rock! There were pot drums, a box guitar and a rice shaker made from a bottle. They had a band name, the Gloop Rockers, and the screen flashed with lights.

The first song started. Bang, bang went the pots! Strum, strum went the box guitar! But the little rice shaker could barely be heard. Shh, shh, shh.

"Nobody can hear me," it sighed. Then, right in the middle of the song, the drums stopped. The guitar stopped. Everything went quiet. It was the rice shaker's turn for a solo!

Shh-shh-shhh-SHAKA-SHAKA-SHAKA! The shaker went wild. It shook fast and slow and loud and soft. The light show flashed in rainbow colors. When it finished, everyone cheered the loudest cheer of the whole night. The rice shaker felt like a real rock star.

title: The Door With a Question Mark
story:
At the very end of a long hallway in the Game Factory, there was a door nobody had noticed before. It was painted bright yellow, with a big question mark in the middle.

Robo knocked. Knock, knock. "Who's there?" said the door. "Robo!" "Robo who?" "Robo who wants to know what's behind you!" The door giggled. "That's a good one! But I can't open yet. I'm saving something special."

Robo sat down on the floor. King Gloop sat down too. Then Baby Gloop, Sammy and Sparks. They took turns telling the door knock-knock jokes. The door laughed at every single one.

When it was time for bed, the door said, "Thank you for keeping me company. Come back soon, okay?" "We will," said Robo. And they all went to bed smiling, wondering what was behind the yellow door.

title: The Surprise Snow Globe
story:
On the windowsill at Moon Base, there was a snow globe. Inside, instead of a snowman or a house, there was just a little golden question mark.

Robo picked it up and gave it a shake. Swirl! Glittery snow danced around the question mark. It sparkled in every color. "Ooh," said Baby Gloop. "What's inside?" "Just a question mark," said Robo. "I think it's a surprise waiting to happen."

They took turns shaking it. Every shake made the glitter swirl a different way. Once it made a heart. Once it looked like a star. Once it looked a little bit like Sammy, which made everyone laugh.

Then they set it back on the windowsill, where the moonlight made it glow. The glitter slowly settled around the little question mark. And everyone went to sleep, dreaming about what it might be.

title: The Gift That Needed Everyone
story:
One day, a giant gift box appeared in the Game Factory. It was so big that Robo couldn't lift it by himself. It had a question mark on every side. "Let me help!" said King Gloop. He pushed. The box didn't budge.

"Me too!" said Sparks. He pulled. The box still didn't budge. One by one, everybody came to help. Baby Gloop, Duke Googool, Nega-Robo and Sammy. They all pushed together. And the box slid across the floor, smooth as ice.

They parked it in the very middle of the room. Then everyone sat down, tired and laughing. "I think that's the trick," said Robo. "This surprise is for everyone, so it takes everyone."

The box gave a little wiggle, as if it agreed. They didn't open it yet. But they all knew that whatever it was, they would enjoy it together.

title: The Sour Lemon Surprise
story:
On a sunny morning, Robo opened a lemonade stand in front of the Game Factory. He had a striped sign, a shiny cash register and a big jug of lemonade. "Grand opening!" he beeped. King Gloop was the very first customer. He took one sip, and his purple face puckered up like a raisin. "SOUR!" he gulped. His crown wobbled right off his head.

Robo's blue eyes blinked. He had forgotten the sugar! He did not want to lose his very first customer. So he did something clever. He gave King Gloop a free cup and asked, "Will you be my taste helper?"

King Gloop loved that job. They stirred in a little sugar, then a little more, and tasted after every spoon. At last King Gloop smiled a wide, gooey smile. "Perfect!" Soon a long line of friends was waiting. Robo counted out the change carefully, and dropped every coin into his piggy bank. The best part? His taste helper got a cup every day for free.

title: The Box on the Tallest Shelf
story:
One morning, Robo found something new on the tallest shelf in the Game Factory. It was a gift box with a shiny ribbon and a big question mark on the side. "A surprise!" Robo beeped. But the shelf was SO high. Robo stretched. He hopped. His antenna wiggled. He still could not reach it.

Baby Gloop bounced over to help, but she was too small. Sammy jumped, but he only reached the second shelf. Then Robo had an idea. "Let's build a tower of friends!"

King Gloop sat at the bottom, squishy and strong. Robo climbed on top of him, and Baby Gloop climbed on top of Robo. She reached up with her little purple arms and pulled the box down gently. Everyone cheered. Robo held the box close and smiled. "This surprise is for the whole family," he said. "We should open it together, with Ben." So they set it on the table, right in the middle, and waited with happy, wiggly feet.

title: Baby Gloop Learns to Wait
story:
Baby Gloop found a box wrapped in sparkly paper. It had a tag that said, "Do not open yet!" Baby Gloop wanted to peek SO badly. Her light purple goo jiggled with excitement. "Just one tiny peek," she whispered. She lifted one corner of the paper. Then she stopped. What if peeking spoiled the surprise for everyone?

She waddled over to King Gloop. "Papa, waiting is SO hard," she said.

King Gloop smiled and straightened his gold crown. "I know a trick," he said. "When waiting is hard, we make waiting fun." So they played a guessing game. Was it as big as a pillow? As small as a button? Was it round, or square, or wobbly? They guessed and giggled until bedtime. Baby Gloop never peeked, not even once. And she found out something wonderful. Wondering about a surprise can be almost as fun as finding it. She fell asleep dreaming of question marks, smiling a sleepy little smile.

title: The Runaway Question Mark Balloon
story:
Robo tied a big red balloon to the mystery box. The balloon was shaped like a question mark, and it bobbed in the breeze. "Now everyone will know a surprise is coming," he said. But then a gust of wind came WHOOSH! The string slipped loose, and the balloon floated up, up, up and away.

"My balloon!" cried Robo. Sparks the robot dog came running, with Charlie and August the cats steering from the driver's seats. "Hop on!" meowed Charlie. Robo climbed onto Sparks's long yellow back, and off they zoomed across the park. The balloon drifted over a pond and through the trees. At last it got caught on the very top of a lamp post.

Sparks stretched his long, long neck. Higher. Higher! He gently grabbed the string with his teeth. They rode home slowly, holding the balloon tight. This time, Robo tied it with a double knot. "Now it can't run away," he said. And the question mark bobbed happily, waiting for the big day.

title: Sammy and the Comfy Box
story:
Everyone was getting the mystery present ready. There was ribbon, tape and a big empty box to put it in. But when Robo turned around, the box was not empty anymore. Sammy was inside it. He was curled up in a brown, stripy ball, and he was purring very loudly.

"Sammy, we need that box for the surprise," said Robo gently. Sammy opened one brown eye. He did not want to move. This box was the comfiest box in the whole world.

Robo did not want to make Sammy sad. So he thought and thought. Then he found another box, just the same size. He put a soft blanket inside it and set it in a warm sunny spot.

Sammy sniffed. He stretched. Then he hopped into the new box and flopped down happily. "Sweet freedom!" he purred. Now everyone had a box. The surprise had its box, and Sammy had his. And when the present was all wrapped up, Sammy was already fast asleep.

title: The Riddle Door
story:
Robo found a map under his pillow. It was covered in little question marks, and they made a trail across the Game Factory. "A treasure hunt!" he beeped. He followed the question marks past the snack room, up the stairs and down a long, twisty hallway. At the end was a small blue door. On the door was a sign. It said, "To open me, answer my riddle: What gets bigger the more you share it?"

Robo scratched his antenna. A cookie gets smaller when you share it. A sandwich does too. Hmm. Then King Gloop came wobbling down the hall. Robo told him about the riddle, and they thought together. King Gloop giggled, and Robo laughed too. Then Robo's blue eyes lit up.

"A smile!" he said. "A smile gets bigger when you share it!" Click! The door opened. Inside was a gift box with a note: "For the whole family. Open together." Robo smiled his biggest smile and carried it home.

title: Duke Googool Guesses
story:
Duke Googool loved being right. So when he saw a mystery box on the table, he lifted his monocle and said, "I shall guess what is inside!" He peered at the box. "It is a teapot!" he said. Robo shook his head. "Nobody knows yet."

"A tuba?" No one knew. "A tiny elephant?" Baby Gloop giggled. "A sandwich that sings?" Now everyone was laughing. Duke Googool frowned under his top hat. "Hmm. Guessing is much harder than I thought."

Then Baby Gloop tugged on his green sleeve. "Your guesses are the funniest ones," she said. "Can you do more?"

Duke Googool smiled a little. Then he smiled a lot. He guessed a rubber duck as big as a bus. He guessed a hat for a giraffe. He guessed a trampoline made of jelly. Nobody found out what was inside that day. But Duke Googool learned something new. Sometimes being silly is even better than being right.

title: No More Wrapping Paper
story:
Robo had a surprise to wrap for the family. He unrolled the wrapping paper and cut, and cut, and cut. Then he stopped. The roll was empty! The box was only half covered. "Oh no," beeped Robo. "The store is closed, and the surprise is tomorrow."

Baby Gloop looked at the box. Then she looked at the crayons on the table. "We can make our OWN paper!" she said. So everyone grabbed a big sheet of plain paper. Robo drew stars. Baby Gloop drew wobbly purple circles. Jimmy, who said he did not want to help, drew one very neat fish with his white paw. Sammy walked across the paint and made little paw prints all over.

Then they wrapped the box in their drawings. It was the most colorful present anyone had ever seen. "I like this better than store paper," said Robo. Jimmy turned away, but his green eyes were proud. And the surprise sat waiting, wrapped in love and question marks.

title: The Missing Dino Bone
story:
Robo was building a dinosaur museum. He brushed fossils out of a big tub of sand, one by one. A long neck bone. A spiky tail. A great big head with lots of teeth. Each time, he heard a mighty ROAR! At last the dinosaur was almost done. But one leg bone was missing. Without it, the dino tipped over with a clatter.

Robo searched the sand. He searched the rice bin and the bean bucket. Nothing. Then he heard a little crunching sound. Sammy was in the corner, happily batting something around with his paw. It was the leg bone! He thought it was a toy.

Robo did not get upset. He just smiled. "Sammy, you're a fossil finder too!" He traded Sammy a crinkly paper ball for the bone, and Sammy was delighted. Robo clicked the leg into place. The dinosaur stood up tall and strong. Robo made a little sign for it. It said: "Found by Robo and Sammy, Museum Explorers."

title: The Wobbly Circle
story:
Baby Gloop wanted to draw Robo. She took a pencil and tried to draw his big round head. But her circle came out wobbly and lumpy. "That's not a circle," she sniffled. "That's a potato." Robo sat down next to her. "Can I tell you a secret?" he asked. "Every drawing starts with one easy step. And wobbly is okay."

He showed her how. First, a light round shape, drawn very softly. Then a dark visor across the middle. Then two blue eyes. Then two ear pods, one on each side. Last of all, a tall antenna with a little ball on top. Baby Gloop tried again, one step at a time. Her circle was still a little bit wobbly. But when she added the visor, the eyes, the ear pods and the antenna, it looked just like Robo!

"It's you!" she cried. Robo laughed. "It's even better than me. My head is wobbly now too." They hung the drawing on the fridge, right in the middle.

title: The Empty Page
story:
Robo wanted to invent a brand new game. He opened his Game Designer Notebook to a clean, empty page. He held his pencil and waited for an idea. He waited. And waited. The page stayed empty. "My brain is out of ideas," he sighed.

King Gloop wobbled over. "Let's spin the Idea Spark machine!" he said. They pulled the lever. Whirr, click, ding! The machine said: "A penguin... on a skateboard... in a volcano." Robo giggled. "That's silly!"

"Silly is a good start," said King Gloop.

So Robo drew a penguin. He gave it a red skateboard. He drew a level map with lava rivers and jumpy rocks. Then King Gloop drew a boss: a giant marshmallow that bounced around. Soon the empty page was full. Then the next one, and the next one. By bedtime they had a whole game planned out. Robo closed his notebook and hugged it. "The hardest part," he said, "was drawing the very first line."

title: The Paper Game Champion
story:
It was rainy at the Game Factory, and the power was flickering. No screens today. "What will we play?" asked Baby Gloop sadly. Robo smiled and pulled out a stack of paper and some pencils. "Paper games!" he said.

First they played Robo Hangman. King Gloop guessed letter after letter, until the word was GOOEY. Then they played Gloop Battleship. Duke Googool hid his ships so cleverly that nobody could find them. Then came Maze Race. Baby Gloop's pencil zoomed through the twists and turns. At the end, Robo counted up all the wins. Oh dear. It was a tie! Everyone had won exactly one game.

"But there can only be one Paper Game Champion," said Duke Googool. Robo thought for a moment. Then he drew a big paper crown and cut it into four pieces. He gave one piece to each friend. "Then we are ALL champions," he said. They taped the crown pieces to their heads and laughed until the rain stopped.

title: The Squiggle That Became a Friend
story:
Robo rolled the Doodle Dice. It landed on "Squiggle Monster!" So Baby Gloop drew a big curly squiggle on a page. "Now you turn it into a monster," she said. Robo looked at the squiggle. He turned the paper this way. He turned it that way. It looked like a mess. "I don't know what to do," he said.

Then he noticed something. One part of the squiggle looked like a nose. Another part looked like a floppy ear. Robo added two googly eyes. Then a smile. Then eight tiny feet with sneakers on. "Ta-da!" he said. "Meet Squigglebert!"

Baby Gloop laughed so hard she rolled off her chair. Squigglebert was the silliest monster ever. So they made another one. And another. Soon there was a whole family of squiggle monsters, and they all needed names. Squigglebert. Wiggly Sue. Captain Loopy. Baby Gloop hung them up in a row. "Squiggles are just friends," she said, "waiting for their faces."

title: Where Is Jimmy's Mouse?
story:
Jimmy had a favorite toy mouse. It was gray and fuzzy, with a long string tail. One morning it was gone. "Hmph," said Jimmy grumpily. He looked under the couch. He looked behind the curtains. No mouse.

Robo came over with a giant Game Factory poster. It was so busy! There were Gloops and robots, karts and candy, stars and spaceships everywhere. "Maybe your mouse got lost in the hidden picture poster," Robo said, with a wink. So Jimmy and Robo searched. They found a hidden banana. They found a tiny umbrella. They found a sleepy fish wearing a hat. They even found a sock on top of a tree.

Then Jimmy's green eyes went wide. There, behind a cupcake in the corner of the poster, was a picture of a little gray mouse. And right behind the real poster, on the floor, was his real toy mouse! Jimmy grabbed it with his white paws. He did not say thank you. But he purred, which meant the very same thing.

title: The Tangled Bow
story:
The mystery present was almost ready. All it needed was a big, fancy bow on top. Robo pulled out a long piece of shiny gold ribbon. He looped it. He twisted it. He tied it. Uh oh. Now the ribbon was one giant knot, as big as a meatball.

"I made a mess," said Robo. He tugged and pulled, but the knot only got tighter. Jimmy watched from the windowsill with his green eyes. He sighed a very loud sigh. Then he hopped down. "Cats," he grumbled, "are experts at string."

Jimmy poked the knot with one white paw. He found a loose end and pulled it gently. Then another. Then another. Slowly, slowly, the knot came undone, until the ribbon was smooth and straight again. Together they tied a beautiful bow. Robo held the box, and Jimmy pressed down the middle with his paw.

"Thank you, Jimmy!" said Robo. "Hmph," said Jimmy. But he sat beside the present all afternoon, guarding his perfect bow.

title: Delivery in the Rain
story:
Robo had an important job. He had to carry a mystery box all the way across town to the family's front door. The box had a ribbon and a big question mark sticker. Halfway there, dark clouds rolled in. Plip. Plop. Then SPLASH! It started to rain.

"Oh no!" said Robo. "The box will get soggy!" He held it under his arm, but the raindrops kept falling. Then a big purple shape came wobbling down the street. It was King Gloop, holding a giant leaf like an umbrella. "Need some help?" he asked.

King Gloop held the leaf high over the box. Robo held the box tight. They walked together, step by step, splashing through puddles.

At last they reached the front door. The box was perfectly dry. Robo and King Gloop were soaking wet, but they did not mind one bit. They set the surprise down on the doormat, rang the bell, and giggled all the way home.

title: Layers and Layers
story:
A little box arrived at the Game Factory. It had a tag that said, "For the family. Unwrap carefully!" Robo pulled off the first layer of paper. Underneath was another layer! And a little note. It said, "You are a great helper."

Robo smiled and pulled off the next layer. Another note: "You make people laugh." Baby Gloop wanted a turn. She peeled the next layer. "You are brave," said the note. Then Sammy batted off a layer with his paw. "You are cozy," the note said, and Sammy purred because it was true.

Layer after layer, note after note. Each one said something kind. Soon there was a big pile of paper on the floor and a big pile of happy friends around it.

At last they reached the very last layer. It had one more note. "The real surprise is still coming. Wait for the whole family!" "Okay," said Robo. He was not even a little bit disappointed. All those kind notes were already a wonderful present.

title: Nega-Robo's Nervous Gift
story:
Nega-Robo was black, with a red visor. A long time ago, he made a lot of trouble. But now he was good, and he wanted to give the family a surprise. He held a box with a big question mark ribbon. But his metal hands were shaking. "What if they don't like it?" he whispered. "What if they remember I used to be naughty?"

Robo rolled up beside him. "Can I tell you something?" said Robo. "Everyone gets nervous sometimes. Even me." "Really?" said Nega-Robo.

"Really. But you know what helps? A friend." Robo held out his hand. So they walked together, side by side, to the family's door. Nega-Robo knocked, very softly. Tap, tap.

The door opened, and there were big smiles everywhere. "For us? Thank you!" Nobody remembered the old trouble. They only saw a friend with a present. Nega-Robo's red visor glowed a little brighter. On the walk home, he was not shaking at all. He was skipping.

title: Chaos Nova Lights the Way
story:
Late one night, Baby Gloop had a terrible thought. She had lost the tag for the mystery present! It said who the surprise was for, and now it was gone. The Game Factory was very dark. Baby Gloop could not see anything at all. "Help!" she called.

Up in the sky, something twinkled. It was Chaos Nova, the rainbow star with one big eye. Chaos Nova floated down, glowing red, then orange, then yellow, then green, blue and purple. "I can help you look," said Chaos Nova.

They searched the halls. The rainbow glow lit up every corner. They looked under the stairs, and behind the toy bin, and inside a boot. Then Chaos Nova's eye spotted something shiny under the rug. The tag!

It said, in big letters: "For the whole family." Baby Gloop hugged Chaos Nova, very carefully, because stars are warm. She tied the tag back on the box with a tight little knot. Then Chaos Nova floated back into the sky and twinkled goodnight.

title: The Biggest Picture Ever
story:
One day, Robo printed the biggest picture the Game Factory had ever seen. It came out of the printer one page at a time, sixteen pages in all. Everyone helped tape the pages together on the floor. King Gloop pressed down the tape. Baby Gloop held the corners. When they were done, the poster was so big it covered the whole room!

Then they grabbed their crayons and started coloring. But there was a problem. Everyone wanted to color the giant Robo in the middle. Robo, King Gloop, Baby Gloop and Sammy all crowded around it, bumping heads. "Ouch!" said Robo. "This isn't working."

Robo had an idea. "Let's each pick our own part," he said. "Then we'll meet in the middle." King Gloop took the castle. Baby Gloop took the candy. They colored and colored until the whole picture was bright. Then they met in the middle and colored giant Robo together, very carefully, all at once.

title: Glint Wraps a Gift
story:
Glint, the mirror robot, wanted to help wrap the family's mystery present. It watched Robo wrap a box in blue paper with white stars. So Glint wrapped its box in blue paper with white stars too. It watched King Gloop tie a purple bow. So Glint tied a purple bow too. Everything Glint made looked exactly like everyone else's.

"Glint," said Robo kindly, "what would YOU like it to look like?" Glint's shiny face flickered. Nobody had ever asked it that before. "I... don't know," it said.

"Let's find out," said Robo. He put out all the papers and ribbons. Glint looked at them for a long, long time. Then it picked silver paper that sparkled like a mirror. It added a ribbon that changed colors in the light. And on top, it drew a tiny question mark that rang like a little glass bell.

Everyone gasped. It was beautiful. "That's so YOU," said Baby Gloop. Glint glowed. It had never felt so much like itself.

title: The Question Mark Cloud
story:
Rocky the gray tabby loved being outside. One afternoon, he was lying in the grass with his friend Mimo, the black cat, watching the clouds float by. "That one looks like a fish," said Rocky.

"That one looks like a sock," said Mimo. Then a very strange cloud drifted over. It was curly at the top, with a little dot underneath. "It's a question mark!" said Rocky.

The cloud floated slowly across the yard. "Let's follow it!" said Mimo. So they did. They crept past the flowers, hopped over the garden hose, and tiptoed past the sleepy bird bath.

The cloud stopped right over the old apple tree. And there, tucked between the roots, was a little box with a ribbon. On top was a card. It said, "Shh! A surprise for the family. Please bring me inside." Rocky and Mimo pushed the box all the way home together, nose by nose. When they looked up, the cloud had turned into a smiley face.

title: The Stuck Countdown Clock
story:
Robo built a countdown clock for the family's big surprise. It had bright red numbers that went down every day. Ten. Nine. Eight. But on the morning it should have said seven, the clock still said eight. Robo tapped it. He shook it. It said eight. "Oh no!" he said. "The surprise clock is stuck!"

Baby Gloop looked worried. "Does that mean the surprise will never come?" "No," said Robo. "It means we need a new way to count." So they made a paper chain instead. Each loop was a different color. Every morning, they would tear off one loop.

The first morning, Baby Gloop tore off the red loop. The next morning, King Gloop tore off the orange loop. Sammy pulled one off with his paw, and Jimmy pretended not to want a turn, then took one anyway. The paper chain got shorter and shorter. Then one morning, the very last loop was gone. Robo smiled. "Today," he said. "Today is the day."

title: The Wobbly Wagon
story:
Robo put the family's mystery box into his red wagon and set off down the path. The wagon rolled along, bump, bump, bump. Then, POP! One of the wheels came right off. It rolled away into the bushes. The wagon tipped over, and the box slid gently onto the grass.

"Oh no," said Robo. "How will I get it home now?" Just then, his friends came along. King Gloop. Baby Gloop. Duke Googool, in his tall top hat. Even Sparks, with Charlie and August in the driver's seats.

"We'll help!" they said.

They looked for the wheel, but it was lost in the bushes. So Duke Googool had a clever idea. He took off his top hat, flipped it upside down and placed the box gently inside it. Then everyone held the brim together, like a parade. Step by step, they carried the surprise all the way home. Baby Gloop sang a marching song. And Duke Googool said it was the most useful his hat had ever been.

title: Sammy Shares the Golden Tuna
story:
One night, Sammy the brown tabby had a wonderful dream. He dreamed about the legendary Golden Tuna. It was shiny and gold, and it smelled like the best dinner ever. When he woke up, Sammy knew he had to find it. He climbed up the bookshelf. He leaped across the kitchen counter. He found a cardboard box and wore it as a disguise. When a guard dog blocked the way, Sammy purred so softly that the dog fell fast asleep.

At last, behind the tenth door, there it was. The Golden Tuna! "Sweet freedom!" said Sammy. But it was big. Much too big for one little cat. Sammy thought about his family. Jimmy, who was a bit grumpy. Rocky, who loved the outdoors. And Mimo, who loved quiet naps.

So Sammy pushed the Golden Tuna all the way home. He shared it into four equal parts. Everyone ate together, purring in a happy row. That night, Sammy dreamed again. This time, he dreamed of all of them, full and cozy.

title: The Missing Answer
story:
Robo loved his puzzle book. There was only one puzzle left, the sudoku on the very last page. Robo filled in the numbers carefully. One, two, three, four. But the last square was tricky. Robo tried a two. No, there was already a two. He tried a three. No, there was a three too.

"Hmm," he said. "I'm stuck." He could flip the book upside down to read the answers. But that would spoil the fun.

So Robo took a break. He looked out the window at the clouds. Then he came back and looked at the puzzle again, with fresh eyes.

And there it was! He had made a little mistake in the row above. He fixed it, and suddenly the last square was easy. It had to be a four! Robo wrote it in and did a happy spin. "Sometimes," he said, "the answer just needs a snack."

title: Stars Shaped Like Question Marks
story:
One quiet night, the cats were looking out the window. Sammy, Jimmy, Rocky and Mimo sat in a row, watching the dark sky. Then something twinkled. A star was moving! It was Tiger, the gentle star cat, padding softly across the sky. Everywhere Tiger stepped, a sparkly paw print appeared.

Tiger began to draw. Curl, curl, dot. A big glowing question mark! Then another one, and another, until the whole sky was full of them. "What does it mean?" asked Rocky.

"I think," said Mimo slowly, "it means a surprise is coming." Jimmy squinted his green eyes. "I don't like waiting," he grumbled.

Tiger heard him, and floated down close to the window. Tiger gave a slow, happy blink, the kind cats give when they love you. Then, with one paw, Tiger drew a tiny heart right next to the question marks. Jimmy blinked back. He did not grumble anymore. The four cats curled up together on the windowsill, warm and sleepy, and dreamed of surprises until morning.

title: Lights, Camera, Gloop!
story:
Robo and his friends were making a funny cartoon movie. Robo held the camera. King Gloop was the star. "Action!" called Robo. King Gloop was supposed to say, "I am the king of the goo!" But every time he opened his mouth, he got the giggles. "I am the king of the... hee hee hee!"

"Cut!" said Robo. They tried again. And again. King Gloop giggled every single time. His crown fell off. His goo jiggled all over. "I'm sorry," said King Gloop, wiping his eyes. "I'm ruining the movie."

Robo looked at the camera. He looked at all the giggly takes. Then he laughed too. "No, you're not!" he said. "This is the funniest movie we've ever made!"

So they put all the giggly parts together. Twelve tries, twelve giggles and one fallen crown. They called it "King Gloop Can't Stop Laughing." On movie night, everyone watched it. And everyone giggled so much that nobody could stop, not even Duke Googool.

title: The Kindness Lock
story:
The family's mystery box had a strange little lock on it. There was no keyhole. There was only a heart-shaped button and a sign. It said, "I open when everyone says something kind." "That's easy!" said Baby Gloop. She pointed at Robo. "You're nice!" The lock went beep, but it did not open.

Robo thought. "I think it wants everyone to take a turn." So they sat in a big circle. Robo said, "King Gloop gives the squishiest hugs." Beep! King Gloop said, "Duke Googool always knows big words." Beep! Duke Googool said, "Baby Gloop has the best giggle in the world." Beep!

Then it was Jimmy's turn. Everyone waited. Jimmy looked away and swished his tail. Finally, very quietly, he said, "Sammy is... a good brother." BEEP!

The heart button glowed bright pink. Click! The lock opened, just a tiny crack. A note peeked out: "Great job. Now save me for the whole family." Sammy purred all afternoon. He had heard every word.

title: The Pillow Lava Problem
story:
Robo turned the whole house into a giant video game. There were paper coins on the stairs and shiny gems under the table. The floor was covered in pillows, and the pillows were LAVA! Baby Gloop hopped from pillow to pillow, collecting coins. She found a power-up card that said, "Super Jump!" She found a save point by the couch. Then she reached the last room.

There was King Gloop, wearing a boss mask, ready for the big battle. But the gap between the last pillow and King Gloop was too far. Even with Super Jump, Baby Gloop could not make it. "I'll never win," she said.

Then she looked at all the coins she had collected. She had an idea! She laid the paper coins down, one by one, like little stepping stones across the lava.

Hop, hop, hop! She made it across. "Boss battle!" she yelled, and tickled King Gloop until he fell over laughing. "You win!" giggled King Gloop. "That was the cleverest move ever."

title: Too Much Goo
story:
King Gloop had a slime lab. It had bubbling bowls, shiny spoons and a big stir-along timer. He loved making slime, because slime reminded him of himself. One day he decided to make the biggest slime ever. He poured in a cup of goo. Then another. Then ten more! He stirred and stirred. The slime grew bigger and bigger, until it spilled over the bowl and oozed across the table.

"Oh no," said King Gloop. "I made TOO much!" Robo peeked in the door. His blue eyes went wide. "Wow," he said. "That's a lot of slime."

King Gloop felt silly. But Robo had an idea. "Let's share it!" They scooped the giant slime into little jars. Purple slime, green slime, sparkly slime. They put a label on each one and gave them to all their friends.

Baby Gloop got the sparkliest jar. Duke Googool got green, to match his top hat. Everyone squished and stretched their slime. "Too much," said King Gloop happily, "turned out to be just right."

title: The Lonely Box
story:
Robo walked past the mystery box late at night. It was sitting all by itself in the dark corner, with its ribbon and its question mark. "Hmm," said Robo. "That box looks a little bit lonely."

Robo knew boxes did not really have feelings. But he still thought it would be nice to keep it company. So he brought over a little lamp, and the corner glowed warm and yellow. Then Baby Gloop came down in her pajamas. "What are you doing?" she whispered.

"Keeping the surprise company," said Robo. Baby Gloop thought that was a wonderful idea. She sat down too. Then Sammy came and curled up beside the box.

Robo sang a soft little song. It was about waiting, and wondering, and good things coming soon. When morning came, the family found everyone asleep in a cozy pile, all around the mystery box. And the box did not look lonely at all.

title: The Volcano That Wouldn't Erupt
story:
Dr. Robo put on his white lab coat and goggles. "Welcome to the Volcano Science Show!" he said. Everyone had built a volcano for the big contest. Baby Gloop's volcano was purple and sparkly. King Gloop's was huge and lumpy. Duke Googool's was very tidy, with a little flag on top.

"Three, two, one, ERUPT!" called Dr. Robo. Baby Gloop's volcano fizzed up with foam. King Gloop's bubbled over. But Duke Googool's volcano did nothing at all. Not a fizz. Not a pop. Duke Googool's monocle drooped. "Oh dear," he said.

Dr. Robo peeked inside. "Aha! You forgot the baking soda," he said kindly. "Every scientist forgets something sometimes. That's how we learn!" Duke Googool added a big scoop of baking soda. "Let's try again!" said Dr. Robo. "Three, two, one..."

WHOOOOSH! Foam shot up so high it splashed Duke Googool's top hat. Everyone cheered. "You win the Bounciest Eruption prize!" said Dr. Robo. And Duke Googool wore his foamy hat proudly all day.

title: Jimmy and the Fluffy Cushion
story:
Jimmy the orange tabby had a fluffy cushion. It was soft and round and smelled just like him. But one morning, it was gone! Someone had taken it to the Game Factory's Lost and Found. "Hmph," said Jimmy. He was very grumpy.

So Jimmy set off on a sneaky trip. Whenever he felt too grumpy, he stopped to nap in a warm sunbeam, and that helped. At last he reached the Lost and Found. There was his cushion! But Baby Gloop was sitting on it, crying softly. She had lost her teddy bear.

Jimmy's tail twitched. He wanted his cushion. But he did not like seeing Baby Gloop sad. So he looked around the Lost and Found. And there, behind a pile of mittens, was a small teddy bear.

Jimmy pushed it to her with his white paw. Baby Gloop hugged the bear and gave Jimmy his cushion back. "Hmph," said Jimmy. But he purred all the way home.

title: The Fish Party Plan
story:
Sammy and Jimmy wanted to throw a surprise fish party for their family. But they needed supplies. Party hats, streamers, and of course, a big plate of fish. The streamers were on a high shelf. "I'll climb!" said Sammy. He jumped, but he could not reach. "Hmph," said Jimmy. "Let me." He jumped. He could not reach either.

The two cats looked at each other. Sammy had an idea. "What if we stack up?" Jimmy did not like being stood on. But he wanted the party to be perfect. So he planted his white paws on the floor, and Sammy climbed carefully on his back. Sammy stretched up high and grabbed the streamers!

Next, they needed to open the fish cupboard. Sammy pulled the lever while Jimmy pushed the door. Together, it worked.

At last, everything was ready. Streamers. Party hats. Fish. When the family walked in, the cats yelled, "SURPRISE!" Everyone cheered. Sammy shouted, "Sweet freedom!" And Jimmy, just this once, did a little happy hop.

title: Baby Gloop the Surprise
story:
Baby Gloop loved surprises so much that she wanted to BE one. She found a big box, climbed inside, and pulled the lid shut. "Now I'm a surprise!" she giggled. She waited for someone to find her. She waited a long time. Then she started to feel a bit sleepy, and a bit hungry, and a bit lonely in the dark box.

Outside, King Gloop was searching everywhere. "Baby Gloop? Where are you?" Robo noticed the box. It had no ribbon and no question mark. But it was wiggling. Robo smiled and knocked gently. Knock, knock.

"Who's there?" said a tiny voice. "A surprise finder," said Robo. He lifted the lid, and out popped Baby Gloop. "SURPRISE!" she shouted. King Gloop laughed and gave her the biggest, gooiest hug.

"You were a great surprise," said King Gloop. "But I like it best when you are right here with me." Baby Gloop agreed. Being a surprise was fun, but being hugged was better. She left the box for the real present.

title: The Question Mark Sticker Hunt
story:
Robo had a sheet of shiny question mark stickers. He wanted to put one on the family's mystery box, but a breeze blew the whole sheet out the window! The stickers scattered everywhere. "Oh no," said Robo. "I need just one!"

So Robo and his friends went on a sticker hunt. Rocky found one stuck to a flower petal. Baby Gloop found one on a puddle. Sparks found one on the end of his own tail. Mimo found one on a sleepy snail's shell. "Should we take it?" asked Mimo. The snail looked very proud of its new sticker. "No," said Robo. "The snail can keep that one."

At the end of the day, they had found lots of stickers. Robo picked the shiniest one and stuck it right in the middle of the box. Then he gave all the others away. One for each friend. Soon everyone was wearing a question mark, and everyone was wondering about the very same surprise.

title: The Slide Delivery
story:
The family's mystery box was at the top of the Game Factory, and the family was waiting at the bottom. The stairs were very long. Robo's legs were very tired. "How can we get it down?" said Robo.

Baby Gloop pointed at the twisty slide. "Wheee!" she said. Robo was not so sure. "What if it bumps?"

So they made the slide extra safe. King Gloop lay at the bottom like a big squishy cushion. Sammy and Jimmy sat at the curves to make sure nothing tipped. Duke Googool held a little flag to say "Go!" Robo set the box gently at the top of the slide. Duke Googool waved the flag. The box went whooooosh around the first curve, around the second curve and plop! It landed safely on King Gloop's soft tummy.

"It worked!" everyone cheered. Then, of course, everyone wanted a turn on the slide too. They slid down one by one until the sun went down, and the surprise waited patiently at the bottom.

title: Lost in the Honeycomb Maze
story:
Robo made a giant maze book. There was a round maze, a star maze and a maze shaped like King Gloop. But his favorite was the honeycomb maze, full of little six-sided rooms. Baby Gloop wanted to try it. She put her finger on the start and went this way, . Then she stopped. "I'm lost," she said. Every room looked the same!

Robo sat beside her. "Here is a maze secret," he said. "Sometimes it helps to start at the end and go backwards." Baby Gloop put her finger on the finish instead. She traced the path back, room by room. Oh! It was much easier from this side. Soon she reached the start.

"I did it!" she cheered. "I solved it backwards!"

Then Baby Gloop wanted to make her own maze. She drew a maze shaped like a big wobbly blob,. It was so twisty that even Robo got lost. "Try going backwards," said Baby Gloop, with a giggle. And it worked!

title: The Story of the Dancing Pickle
story:
Robo had a story with blank spaces in it. "Let's fill in silly words!" he said. King Gloop tapped a picture of a pickle. Baby Gloop tapped "dancing." Duke Googool tapped "underpants." Then Robo pressed play, and the story read out loud. "Once upon a time, a dancing pickle lost his underpants!"

Everyone laughed so hard. But then Duke Googool frowned. "That's not a REAL story," he said. "It doesn't make sense." Robo thought about it. "Maybe it can make sense. What would a pickle do if he lost his underpants?"

"He would look for them," said Baby Gloop. "Under the lettuce!" said King Gloop. "And ask a wise old carrot for help," said Duke Googool, starting to smile.

So they kept going, adding more and more. The dancing pickle searched the whole fridge, made friends with a carrot and found his underpants on a cupcake. Then he danced all the way home. "That," said Duke Googool, "is my favorite story ever."

title: The Monster Nobody Wanted to Draw
story:
Robo rolled the dice. "Seven eyes!" he said. He rolled again. "Noodle arms!" Again. "Wheels for feet!" Again. "A tutu!" He grabbed his pencil and drew the monster. Seven eyes. Wiggly noodle arms. Little round wheels. And a pink tutu. It was the strangest monster ever.

"Eww," said Baby Gloop. "It looks weird." Robo looked at his drawing. The monster did look a little weird. Then Robo had an idea. He drew a big smile on its face. He drew a balloon in one noodle arm. He drew a little party hat on top.

Now the monster looked friendly. In fact, it looked like it was going to a party. "Oh!" said Baby Gloop. "He's not weird. He's fancy!"

They named him Sir Wheelie Tutu. Baby Gloop rolled the dice next, and her monster had three tails and a mustache. They drew Sir Wheelie a best friend. By bedtime there was a whole monster party on the table, and every monster was smiling.

title: The Sock-Finding Machine
story:
Duke Googool had a problem. Every morning, one of his socks was missing. "Where do all the socks GO?" he cried. Robo opened his Inventor's Sketchbook. "Let's invent a machine to find them!" They spun the Idea Machine.

"How strange," said Duke Googool. But they started drawing anyway. A big fan to blow under the bed. A long arm to reach behind the dresser. And a rubber chicken on top that squawked whenever a sock was found. They built it out of boxes and string. Robo flipped the switch. The fan whirred. The arm wiggled. And then... SQUAWK! The chicken honked loudly.

Out came a sock from under the bed. SQUAWK! Another sock from behind the dresser. SQUAWK, SQUAWK!

And then out came Sammy, holding a sock in his mouth. He had been collecting them all along, to make a cozy nest. Duke Googool laughed and let Sammy keep one. "Every inventor needs a helper," he said.

title: The Level Nobody Could Beat
story:
Robo loved drawing paper platformer levels. He drew hills, holes and floating blocks. Then his friends used a pencil to draw his path, jump by jump. One day, King Gloop made a level for Robo to solve. It had a giant pit, a spiky wall and a floating platform way up high.

Robo used the cut-out jump ruler. He measured the first jump. Too far! He tried a different path. He tried every way, but he could not reach the end. "King Gloop," said Robo, "I don't think this level can be beaten."

King Gloop looked at his drawing. He measured it with the jump ruler too. "Oops," he said. "You're right. I made the pit too big!" He felt a little bit embarrassed. But Robo said, "That's how real game designers learn. They test their levels!"

So King Gloop drew a little cloud right over the pit, for Robo to bounce on. Robo tried again. Jump, bounce, jump! He made it to the flag. "Now it's perfect," said Robo.

title: The Mystery Picture
story:
Baby Gloop opened the Color-by-Number Book to a mystery page. It was just a lot of little shapes with numbers in them. "What is it?" she asked. "Nobody knows until you color it," said Robo. "One means red. Two means blue. Three means yellow."

Baby Gloop started coloring. But she got excited and colored a number two space bright purple, because purple was her favorite. "Oops," she said. "Now it's wrong." Robo looked at it. "Hmm. Let's see what happens," he said.

Baby Gloop kept coloring, red, blue and yellow, and one purple space. Slowly, a picture appeared. It was a rocket ship flying through space! And right in the window, where she had used purple, it looked like a little purple Gloop was driving! "Look!" she said. "I'm the pilot!"

Robo laughed. "That's the best mistake ever." Baby Gloop hung the rocket picture above her bed. Every night, she looked at it and imagined herself flying to the stars.

title: Robo's Big Question
story:
Robo wanted to ask everyone a question. He took a clipboard and a pencil. "What is your favorite snack?" he asked. King Gloop said, "Jelly!" Robo made a tally mark. Baby Gloop said, "Jelly!" Another tally. Duke Googool said, "Crackers, of course." Sammy said "Fish," by meowing very loudly, and Robo counted that too.

Then Robo made a bar graph. The jelly bar was tallest. The crackers bar and the fish bar were short. Duke Googool looked at the graph and frowned. "Only one person likes crackers," he said. "Nobody likes the same things as me."

Robo thought about it. Then he made another survey. "What is your favorite color?" This time, Duke Googool said green. And so did Rocky, who loved the grass. And so did Jimmy, whose eyes were green. The green bar grew and grew! It was the tallest bar of all.

Duke Googool's monocle sparkled. "Three friends like green, like me!" "See?" said Robo. "Everyone matches somebody, somewhere."

title: Jimmy's Name Sign
story:
Everyone at the Game Factory was making door signs with bubble letters. Robo made his in shiny robot letters. Baby Gloop made hers in gooey drippy letters. King Gloop's had a crown on every letter. Jimmy sat on the windowsill. "I don't need a sign," he said grumpily. "Everyone knows where I sleep."

But when nobody was looking, Jimmy peeked at all the signs. They were so colorful. Jimmy's tail twitched. He did kind of want one. Robo noticed. He did not say anything. He just left a piece of paper and some orange crayons next to Jimmy.

Later that night, Jimmy tried. He drew a big puffy J. It was a little lopsided. He drew a puffy I, two puffy Ms and a Y. Then he added little paw prints and a fish on top. In the morning, there was a new sign on Jimmy's cushion. It said JIMMY in big, orange bubble letters.

"Nice sign," said Robo. "Hmph," said Jimmy. But he slept right under it, very proudly.

title: The Gloop Who Just Wanted a Snack
story:
The Gloops were marching toward the Game Factory door again. Robo and his friends were ready. Sammy, Jimmy and Robo stood like towers along the path. "Here they come!" said Robo. The little Gloops bounced away. Then came a very small Gloop, slower than the others. It was not trying to sneak in. It was just looking around with big hungry eyes.

Robo held up his hand. "Wait!" he said. "Don't bonk that one." He rolled over to the little Gloop. "Why are you trying to get into the Game Factory?"

"I smelled cookies," said the little Gloop. "I'm so hungry." Robo felt bad. Maybe the Gloops did not want trouble. Maybe they just wanted a snack. So Robo opened the door and brought out a big plate of cookies.

The little Gloop gobbled one. Then all the other Gloops came marching back, not to sneak in, but to say please. That day, there was no battle. There was just a very big picnic.

title: The Monster With Everyone in It
story:
It was family game night, and everyone was playing Pass-the-Picture. Robo folded the paper into three parts. "I'll draw the head," he said. "No peeking!" Robo drew a robot head with an antenna. He folded it over and passed it to King Gloop. King Gloop drew a big gooey belly with a crown on it. He folded it over and passed it to Baby Gloop. She drew legs, but she drew them as kitten paws, because she loved Sammy.

Then it was time for the big reveal. "One, two, three, UNFOLD!" Everyone gasped. Then they laughed so hard they fell off their chairs. The monster had Robo's head, King Gloop's belly and Sammy's paws!

But Baby Gloop stopped laughing. "Oh no," she said. "The legs don't connect to the belly. I drew them too far apart."

Robo grabbed a crayon. "Then let's give him springs!" he said. He drew bouncy springs between the belly and the paws. They named him Robo-Gloop-Sammy-Boing. And he became the family's favorite monster, forever.

title: The Door That Wanted a Friend
story:
Lock Robo used to lock things up and cause trouble. But now Lock Robo was nice. He had built a cozy Puzzle Vault with 48 doors, and behind each door was a treasure. Robo came to visit. He slid keys, turned gears and cracked codes. Door after door swung open. Gold coins! Shiny gems!

But door number 48 would not open. Robo tried every key. Nothing worked. "Lock Robo," said Robo, "how do I open this one?"

Lock Robo looked at his feet. "That door has no puzzle," he said quietly. "I just... didn't want you to leave yet. That's my favorite treasure, and I wanted to share it with a friend." Robo smiled. "Then let's open it together."

Lock Robo turned the handle. Inside was a little table with two cups of cocoa and a board game. It was his treasure: a game night with a friend. They played until it was very late. And Robo promised to come back every week.

title: The Picture Hidden in the Squares
story:
Robo found a strange paper in his mailbox. It had a big grid of empty squares, letters across the top and numbers down the side. At the bottom were clues. "Color B4. Color C4. Color D5." "A secret grid picture!" beeped Robo. He sat down and colored square after square. Slowly, a shape appeared. It looked like a fish! Then he colored more. It had a tail and a crown!

"A fish with a crown?" said Robo. "Who would send this?" He looked at the last clue. It said, "Go to G7." Robo found G7 on the grid. Next to it was a tiny drawing of the pond behind the Game Factory.

Robo walked to the pond. There, sitting on a rock, was Baby Gloop, wearing a paper crown and holding a paper fish. "Surprise!" she shouted. "I made a secret grid for you!"

"You're the Fish Queen!" Robo laughed. Then Robo made a secret grid for her, and it hid a picture of the two of them, holding hands.

title: How Tall Is King Gloop?
story:
Robo had a brand new Robo Ruler. "Time for a measuring mission!" he said. He measured the table. He measured his own antenna. Then Baby Gloop asked a big question. "How tall is King Gloop?"

Robo held up the ruler to King Gloop. But King Gloop was made of goo. When he took a breath, he got taller. When he sat down, he got shorter and wider. "Stand still!" said Robo. But King Gloop could not stop jiggling.

Robo thought for a moment. Then he had an idea. "Let's measure you three times," he said. "Once tall, once squishy and once laughing!" Tall King Gloop was 30 inches. Squishy King Gloop was 15 inches. And Laughing King Gloop changed so much that nobody could measure him at all.

They wrote it all down on a big chart. "King Gloop: 15 to 30 inches, depending on his mood." King Gloop was very proud. "I'm the only friend who comes in three sizes!"

title: The Secret Knock
story:
The mystery box was hidden in a special room. To get in, you had to know the secret knock. Robo made it up. Knock-knock, knock, knock-knock-knock! But on the big day, Robo forgot it. "Was it knock, knock-knock? Or knock-knock-knock, knock?" He tried and tried, but the door would not open.

"Oh dear," he said. "The family's surprise is stuck inside." Then he heard a sound. Thump-thump, thump, thump-thump-thump. It was coming from Sparks's tail! The robot dog was wagging it against the floor. Charlie and August had been listening the first time, and they taught Sparks the rhythm.

"That's it!" cried Robo. "That's the knock!"

Robo copied the beat on the door. Knock-knock, knock, knock-knock-knock! Click! The door swung open. There was the mystery box, safe and sound. Robo gave Sparks a big pat on the head, and Charlie and August each got a treat. "From now on," said Robo, "you three are the official knock keepers."

title: The Confetti Trail
story:
Someone had left a trail of colorful confetti across the Game Factory floor. Little pieces of red, yellow, green and blue went all the way down the hall. Sparks sniffed it. "A trail!" said Charlie, from the driver's seat. "Let's follow it!" said August.

So off they went. The confetti led past the kitchen and up the ramp. Then it went right through a big puddle! The puddle had washed some of the confetti away. "Oh no," said Charlie. "We lost the trail."

Sparks sniffed and sniffed. He could not find the next piece. Then August had a clever idea. "Look up!" A few pieces of confetti were stuck on the ceiling fan. They pointed toward the back door.

Sparks zoomed outside. And there on the porch, under a little umbrella, was a mystery box with a big question mark. A note said: "You found me! Please keep me safe for the family." Sparks wagged his purple tail so hard that confetti flew everywhere.

title: Jimmy the Guard
story:
Robo had to go out for a little while. "Somebody needs to guard the family's mystery box," he said. "Who will do it?" Nobody answered. Then Jimmy yawned. "I suppose I could," he grumbled. "But only because the box is next to my sunbeam."

So Jimmy sat beside the box. Baby Gloop bounced by. "Can I shake it?" she asked. "No," said Jimmy. Duke Googool came by with a magnifying glass. "May I take a closer look?" "No," said Jimmy. Then Sammy came by and tried to sit on top of the box. Jimmy gave him a look. Sammy hopped right off.

Jimmy was a very good guard. Nobody peeked. Nobody shook. Nobody sat on it.

When Robo came home, the box was perfect. "Jimmy, you did it!" said Robo. "You're the best guard in the Game Factory!" He gave Jimmy a shiny paper badge that said GUARD CAT. "Hmph," said Jimmy. But he wore the badge all week, even while he napped.

title: Two Hundred Dots
story:
Baby Gloop opened the Mega Dot-to-Dot Book. The first page had a few dots. Easy! The second page had more. But the last page had TWO HUNDRED dots! They were tiny and close together, like sprinkles. "That's too many," said Baby Gloop. "I can't do two hundred."

"You don't have to do them all at once," said Robo. "Just do ten. Then take a break." So Baby Gloop connected dots one to ten. It looked like a little curve. She had a cracker. Then she did eleven to twenty. Now it looked like a bumpy line. She had a drink of water.

Twenty-one to fifty. Fifty-one to a hundred. She was getting faster! A shape was appearing. Something round, with a long stick on top. One hundred and fifty. One hundred and ninety. One hundred and ninety-nine... and two hundred! It was Robo! His round head, his visor, his ear pods and his antenna.

"You drew me!" said Robo. "With two hundred tiny steps," said Baby Gloop, very proudly.

title: Where Does the Shadow Go?
story:
Robo wanted his drawing of a ball to look round, like a real ball. But it just looked flat, like a circle. "How do I make it pop out?" he asked. King Gloop knew a trick. "Shading!" he said. "Pretend there is a sun in the corner of the page. The side near the sun is bright. The side far away is dark."

Robo drew a little sun in the top corner. Then he shaded the bottom of the ball, far from the sun. But he forgot which way the sun was, and shaded the top too. Now the ball looked like it was in a cave! King Gloop got a flashlight. He shined it on a real orange from the kitchen. "Look," he said. "The light hits the top. The shadow falls on the bottom."

Robo looked at the orange. Then he drew again, slowly. The ball looked round! They celebrated by eating the orange.

title: The Broken Streak
story:
Robo had been drawing every single day. On Monday he drew a pizza wearing sunglasses. On Tuesday he drew a whale on a bicycle. Every day, his streak got bigger. Seven days! Eight days! Nine! But on the tenth day, Robo was very busy. He helped King Gloop fix a leaky pipe. He played tag with Baby Gloop. He gave Sammy a bath, which took a long, long time. When bedtime came, Robo realized he had forgotten to draw.

His streak was gone. Back to zero. Robo's blue eyes drooped. Baby Gloop patted his arm. "But you helped everyone today," she said. "That's a good thing too."

Robo thought about it. Then he smiled. The next morning, he got a new drawing idea: "Draw your favorite day." Robo knew exactly what to draw. He drew the busy day. The pipe, the tag game and a very soapy Sammy. It was his favorite drawing of all. His streak started again at one, and one felt just right.

title: What Could It Be?
story:
Robo zoomed in so close on a picture that it was just a blob of bright orange with a white curve. "What is it?" he asked his friends. "A carrot!" said Baby Gloop.

"A sunset," said Duke Googool. "A goldfish," said King Gloop, licking his lips.

Robo zoomed out one step. Now there was more orange, with some stripes, and a little pink spot. "A tiger!" said Baby Gloop. "A striped sock!" said King Gloop. Robo zoomed out again. Now they could see whiskers. And a white paw. And a very grumpy green eye. Everyone shouted at once. "It's JIMMY!" Jimmy was sitting right behind them on the couch. He had heard everything. "A goldfish?" he said, flicking his tail.

Everyone giggled. Then they had an idea. They took a photo of Jimmy's nose, zoomed way in, and played the game again with the rest of the family. Nobody guessed it. Jimmy acted annoyed. But secretly, he liked being the star of the game.

title: Robo Learns to Jump
story:
Robo wanted to make a flip book of himself doing a big jump. He drew the first page. Robo standing still. He drew the second page. Robo bending his knees. Then page three, Robo in the air. He flipped the pages fast. Flip, flip, flip! But Robo did not jump smoothly. He just blinked from one place to another, like a hiccup.

"Hmm," said Robo. "That doesn't look right." "I know what's wrong!" he said. "Each page is too different. I need more tiny steps in between."

So he drew more pages. Twenty pages in all, each one only a tiny bit different.

He flipped them again. Flip-flip-flip-flip! Robo jumped up smoothly into the air and came down with a little bounce. "It works!" he cheered. Then he drew one more page: Sammy, cheering too.

title: Robo's Mixed-Up Face
story:
Robo was learning to draw feelings. Happy eyes curved up. Sad eyes drooped down. Surprised eyes were big and round. He drew 24 faces in a row. Then King Gloop came in. He was not smiling or frowning. His face was a little bit of everything.

"What's wrong?" asked Robo. "I don't know," said King Gloop. "I'm excited because Baby Gloop starts swimming lessons tomorrow. But I'm worried too. And a little bit proud. My face doesn't know what to do."

Robo looked at his drawings. None of them matched. So he grabbed a pencil. He drew one excited eye, one worried eyebrow and a proud little smile, all together on one face. "That's me!" said King Gloop. "A mixed-up face!"

"You can have lots of feelings at once," said Robo. "That's normal. It just means you care a lot." King Gloop felt better. He hung the mixed-up face on the fridge. The next day, after swimming lessons, they drew a new one. It was just plain, happy and proud.

title: The Number Two Swan
story:
Baby Gloop was practicing her numbers. She wrote a one. She wrote a two. But her two was very curvy, with a long swoosh at the bottom. "That doesn't look like a two," she sighed. "It looks like a bird."
