Robo looked at it. "You're right," he said, with a twinkle. "Let's MAKE it a bird!" He showed her how. Add a little dot for an eye. Add a beak on the tip.

Baby Gloop gasped. "It's a swan!" Now she wanted to try every number. Her eight became a snowman with a carrot nose. Her three turned sideways and became the top of a bumblebee. Her zero became Robo's round head, with an antenna on top.

By the end of the day, she had a whole page of number doodles. And she had written every number from one to ten, many, many times, without even noticing. "Numbers," said Baby Gloop happily, "are just doodles in disguise."

title: The Lines That Played a Trick
story:
Duke Googool was very clever. He always said, "My eyes are never fooled!" So Robo brought him to Optical Illusion School. Robo drew two lines. One had arrows pointing in. One had arrows pointing out. "Which line is longer?" he asked.

Duke Googool raised his monocle. "The top one, obviously." Robo held up a ruler. The lines were exactly the same size! Duke Googool's mouth fell open. "Impossible!"

Then Robo showed him a drawing of a cube that seemed to flip inside out. A spiral that seemed to spin. A picture that was a vase, or two faces, depending on how you looked. Duke Googool's monocle popped right off. "My eyes ARE fooled!" he said. "Every single time!"

At first, he felt a little silly. But then he started to laugh. "This is wonderful," he said. "Brains are full of surprises." Duke Googool learned to draw his own illusion. He showed it to King Gloop, who was fooled too. And they giggled together like two little Gloops.

title: The Paper Airplane Invitation
story:
Robo was sitting in the garden when something swooped over his head. Zoom! It was a paper airplane. It did a loop-the-loop and landed right in his lap. Robo unfolded it. Inside was a drawing of a question mark and some words. "You are invited to a SURPRISE. Bring your family. Fly this note to a friend!"

Robo smiled. He folded the paper back into a plane, aimed carefully and threw it. Whoosh! But it went the wrong way. It flew right into the top of a tree. "Oh no," said Robo. "The invitation is stuck!"

Just then, Rocky came strolling by. Rocky was the best climber in the whole Game Factory. "I'll get it!" he said. Up the tree he went, paw over paw, to the very top branch. He grabbed the plane in his mouth.

Rocky climbed back down. Then he gave the plane a gentle toss to Mimo. Soon everyone knew. A surprise was coming. And everyone was invited.

title: The Mystery Beep
story:
Robo's antenna started to beep. Beep. Beep. Beep. "What's that?" he wondered. He had never heard that sound before. He turned left. The beeping got quieter. He turned right. The beeping got louder! "It's leading me somewhere," said Robo.

He followed the beeps through the Game Factory. Into the music room. Beep, beep, beep! Louder and louder! But the music room was full of drums, horns and bells. Robo looked everywhere. Which one was beeping?

He asked King Gloop, Baby Gloop and Duke Googool to be very, very quiet. Nobody moved. Nobody breathed. And then Robo heard it. A tiny ding, coming from a little silver bell on the top shelf.

Next to the bell was a box with a big question mark on it. The bell was tied to the ribbon. It was a surprise bell, ringing to be found! Robo carried the box down carefully. It was for the family. And now that it was found, the bell rang one last happy ding.

title: The Key in the Sandbox
story:
Baby Gloop was building a sandcastle. She dug a moat. She made a tower. Then her little shovel went clink! It hit something hard. She brushed away the sand. It was a key! A shiny gold key, shaped like a question mark.

"What does it open?" asked Baby Gloop. She ran to show King Gloop. King Gloop looked at the key and smiled. "I think it opens something very special. But we must find the lock."

They tried the front door. It did not fit. They tried the cookie jar. Nope. They tried Duke Googool's suitcase, and he got very nervous about that. Then Robo remembered something. In the attic, there was an old wooden chest with a funny curly keyhole. They climbed up together. Baby Gloop held up the key. It fit perfectly!

Inside the chest was a note. "Well done, explorers! The surprise is ready for the whole family. Go get them!" Baby Gloop slid down the stairs on her belly, shouting, "Everyone! Come quick!"

title: Glint Finishes the Butterfly
story:
Glint, the mirror robot, was very good at copying. So when Robo found a page with half a butterfly drawn on it, he asked Glint for help. "Can you draw the other half?" Glint looked at the left wing. Glint copied it perfectly onto the right side. The butterfly was perfectly matched.

"Wow!" said Robo. "It's perfect!" But Glint did not look happy. "I only copied," it said quietly. "I always copy."

Robo thought. "What if you draw your own butterfly? A brand new one. Then I'll try to copy YOU." Glint had never done that before. It picked up a pencil. It drew one wing with stars on it, and a little musical note, and a stripe like a rainbow. Then it handed the paper to Robo.

Robo tried to draw the other half. His stars were wobbly,. But he did his best. The butterfly was not perfectly matched anymore. But Glint thought it was the most beautiful one of all.

title: The Monster Who Needed a Name
story:
The family folded a paper into three parts. Robo drew a monster head with antlers. King Gloop drew a body covered in polka dots. Sammy drew the legs, holding the crayon in his mouth, which made them very squiggly. They unfolded it. "Ta-da!" There was a silly monster with antlers, polka dots and squiggly legs.

"Now it needs a name," said Robo. They spun the name spinner. It landed on "Sir Snorkelpants." Everyone laughed. But Baby Gloop shook her head. "He doesn't look like a Snorkelpants." They spun again. "Captain Noodlebeard." "No," said Baby Gloop. "Princess Waffle." "Nope."

"Well, what DOES he look like?" asked King Gloop.

Baby Gloop looked at the monster for a long time. The squiggly legs looked like they were dancing. The antlers looked like he was happy. "He looks like a Wiggles," she said. Everyone agreed. It was perfect. They hung Wiggles on the wall. And every time they made a new monster after that, Baby Gloop got to pick the name.

title: The Wise Owl's Secret
story:
Robo was trying to trace a picture of a little house. The rule was: draw the whole thing in one line, without lifting your pencil. He started at the roof. He went down the wall. Then he got stuck. He had to lift his pencil! "This is impossible," Robo sighed.

Then a soft voice said, "Hoo, hoo." It was the Wise Owl, sitting on a branch by the window. "Would you like to know my secret?" Robo nodded.

"Count the lines that meet at each corner," said the Owl. "If a corner has an odd number, like one or three, start there. That is the secret door." Robo counted. Most corners had two or four lines. But two corners at the bottom had three. "Start at one of those," said the Owl.

Robo put his pencil on the bottom corner. and he never lifted his pencil once! "I did it!" Robo cheered. The Owl blinked slowly, very pleased. "Hoo, hoo. Well done."

title: The Slow and Steady Kart
story:
Robo, Sammy and King Gloop were racing pencil cars on a graph-paper racetrack. Each turn, you moved your car from dot to dot. You could go faster and faster. But if you went too fast, you might crash at the turns. King Gloop went super fast right away. Zoom, zoom! Sammy went fast too. But Robo went slowly and carefully, one dot at a time.

"Robo, you're so far behind!" giggled King Gloop. Then they reached the big curve. King Gloop was going so fast he could not turn. Crash! He went right off the track into the grass. Sammy tried to turn and spun around in a circle. Crash!

Robo came around the curve, slow and steady. He turned perfectly. Then he sped up on the straight part, faster and faster, and crossed the finish line first! "How did you do that?" asked King Gloop.

"I slowed down for the curves," said Robo. "Then I zoomed." Next race, everyone tried it. And this time it was a three-way tie.

title: Too Many Stripes
story:
Baby Gloop loved stripes. At the Pattern Party, she colored a big picture of a dragon. She gave it stripes on its wings. Stripes on its tail. Stripes on its tummy. When she was done, she frowned. "It doesn't look like a dragon anymore," she said. "It looks like a stripy blob."

Robo looked at it. "Maybe it needs some other patterns, so the stripes can shine," he said. "Like a friend for your stripes." So Baby Gloop tried. She left the stripes on the wings. Then she drew polka dots on the tummy. Little zigzags on the tail, like spikes. And tiny hearts on the face, because this was a nice dragon.

Now every part of the dragon looked different. And somehow, the stripes looked even better!

"Oh!" said Baby Gloop. "Patterns are like friends. They look best together." She colored a whole page of Robo next,. Then she made King Gloop all checkered. He said he looked like a picnic blanket, and he loved it.

title: The Cat That Became a Cloud
story:
Everyone sat in a circle for Doodle Telephone. Robo went first. He drew a cat sitting in a box. He showed it to King Gloop, and only King Gloop. King Gloop whispered to Baby Gloop, "A cat in a box." But he whispered so softly that Baby Gloop heard, "A hat on a fox." So she drew a fox wearing a fancy hat.

She showed the fox to Duke Googool. Duke Googool thought the fox looked fluffy, so he whispered to Sammy, "A fluffy cloud." Sammy drew a cloud,. Then it was time for the BIG REVEAL! Robo showed his cat in a box. Then the fox in a hat. Then the cloud.

"How did a cat turn into a cloud?" asked Robo. Everyone laughed until their tummies hurt. But Duke Googool looked worried. "Did I ruin it?"

"No!" said Robo. "That's the whole fun. The silly mistakes make the best stories." So they played again. That time, a dinosaur turned into a banana.

title: The Bounciest Shoes
story:
Robo wanted to design the best sneakers ever. He gave them rocket boosters. He gave them wings. He gave them light-up soles that flashed every color. He put them on and went to the test track. "Three, two, one, GO!" Whoosh! The rocket boosters were so strong that Robo zoomed right off the track and landed in a bush.

"Too fast," said Robo, picking a leaf off his antenna. Baby Gloop was watching. "Maybe try springs instead?" she said.

So Robo took off the rockets and put springs on the bottom. He tried the track again. Boing! Boing! BOING! Now he was bouncing so high he could not steer. Robo sat down and thought. Rockets were too fast. Springs were too bouncy. Then he smiled. "What about just a little of each?"

He made new sneakers with tiny springs and baby rockets. He ran the track again. Boing, whoosh, boing, whoosh! It was perfect. Robo won the race. Then he made a smaller pair, with sparkles, just for Baby Gloop.

title: Gloopy O's
story:
King Gloop wanted to invent a breakfast cereal. "It will be called Gloopy O's," he said. "Little purple rings, with gold crown marshmallows!" He drew the box. He wrote the name in big bubbly letters. He added a maze on the back and a fun fact on the side. Then he filmed a TV commercial. "Gloopy O's! The goo-ey-est breakfast in town!"

But when he showed the commercial to Robo, Robo looked puzzled. "Goo-ey cereal? Doesn't cereal need to be crunchy?" King Gloop's crown drooped. "Oh no. Nobody wants soggy cereal."

Then Baby Gloop had an idea. "What if it's crunchy on the outside... and gooey on the inside? Like a surprise!" King Gloop's face lit up. He changed the box. Now it said: "Crunchy outside! Gooey surprise inside!" He filmed a new commercial, with Baby Gloop crunching and giggling.

Everyone wanted to try it. Robo poured a pretend bowl. "Crunch, crunch... squish!" he said. "Delicious!" And Baby Gloop's face went right on the front of the box.

title: Drawing a Song
story:
Robo turned on some music. It was slow and soft, like falling snow. "Draw what the music feels like," he said. Baby Gloop drew gentle blue swirls. Then the music changed. It got fast and bouncy! Everyone drew zigzags and stars and jumping frogs.

But Jimmy sat in the corner, not drawing. "Music doesn't have a shape," he grumbled. Robo put on a new song. It was a slow, warm, sleepy tune, like a sunbeam on a quiet afternoon. Jimmy's ears twitched. His tail swished slowly from side to side.

"What does this one feel like?" Robo asked softly. Jimmy did not answer. He just took a crayon in his white paw and drew a big yellow circle. Then long yellow lines going down. Then a little orange shape, curled up in the middle. It was a sunbeam, with a cat napping in it.

"That's the song exactly!" said Robo. "Hmph," said Jimmy. Then he curled up and napped, just like his drawing.

title: The Hero's Silly Weakness
story:
Robo was helping Baby Gloop make herself into a Game Factory hero. "What's your super power?" he asked. "Super bounce!" said Baby Gloop. "And I can stretch really, really far!"

Robo wrote it down. "Every hero also needs a silly weakness," he said. "Like how I get dizzy when I spin too fast." Baby Gloop thought and thought. She did not want a weakness. Then she remembered something. "I get the giggles when someone tickles me," she said. "And then I can't bounce at all."

"Perfect!" said Robo. Then they drew her first adventure. A big boss was attacking the Game Factory. the boss reached out and... tickled her! Baby Gloop giggled so hard she fell over. But her giggle was so loud and so happy that the boss started giggling too. Soon the boss was laughing too much to fight anymore.

"Your weakness saved the day!" said Robo. Baby Gloop drew a gold medal on her character sheet. "Giggle Power," she wrote.

title: The Fizziest Drink
story:
Robo and Baby Gloop were inventing a pretend drink. "Let's put in strawberry," said Baby Gloop. "And banana," said Robo. "And bubbles!" they both said. They mixed it in a big fizzy bottle. It turned bright pink. Then they added more bubbles. And more. And MORE!

The bottle started to wobble. Fizz, fizz, FIZZ! Then POP! The cap flew off, and pretend pink bubbles shot up to the ceiling. "Oops," said Robo, covered in pretend foam.

They tried again with just a little bit of bubbles. It was nice, but it did not tickle their noses. "Too fizzy was too much," said Baby Gloop. "Not fizzy enough is boring." So they set up a family taste test. King Gloop tried three bottles. Duke Googool tried three bottles. Even Sammy sniffed them all.

Everybody picked the middle one. Just the right amount of fizz! They called it "Pink Pop Party." They drew it on a juice box, with a paper straw. And the ceiling? It stayed pretend pink for weeks.

title: The Golden Ticket Mix-Up
story:
Duke Googool invented a candy bar. It was called the Choco-Monocle. It was round, with a crunchy middle, and the wrapper had a picture of him tipping his top hat. "Somewhere, in one wrapper, I will hide a golden ticket," he said. He made a hundred wrappers. He hid the ticket in one of them. Then he mixed them all up.

But later, he couldn't remember which one it was! And he had promised the ticket to Baby Gloop for her birthday. "Oh dear, oh dear," said Duke Googool. He unwrapped five candy bars. No ticket. Ten candy bars. No ticket.

Robo came over. "Can I help?" he said. He held each wrapper up to the light. Most wrappers looked dark. But one wrapper glowed a little, right in the middle. "That's it!" said Robo. Inside was the golden ticket!

Duke Googool gave it to Baby Gloop with a bow. She squealed with joy. And all those unwrapped candy bars? They shared them at the party. Nobody minded one bit.

title: The Toy That Did Nothing
story:
Robo was inventing toys. He made a robot that walked. He made a car that flew. He made a ball that sang. Every toy did something amazing. Then Baby Gloop showed him her invention. It was a simple soft square, with a smiley face drawn on it. "It's called Squishy Buddy," she said.

Robo looked at it. "What does it do?" "Nothing," said Baby Gloop. "You just hold it."

Robo did not want to hurt her feelings. But he wondered if anyone would like a toy that did nothing. They opened their pretend Toy Store. Customers came in. They played with the walking robot. They chased the flying car. They listened to the singing ball. But at bedtime, every customer came back. They all asked for the same thing. "Do you have a Squishy Buddy? Something to hug while we sleep?"

Baby Gloop sold every single one. Robo laughed. "You invented the best toy of all," he said. That night, Robo fell asleep holding a Squishy Buddy too.

title: The Game With No Name
story:
Robo designed his very own video game. It had a hero who could fly, a dragon who loved soup and a castle made of pancakes. He drew the case cover, made a game disc and put it on his Game Shelf. But there was one problem. The game had no name.

"Call it Flying Hero," said King Gloop. Robo shook his head. "Too boring." "Call it The Magnificent Saga of the Brave Aviator," said Duke Googool. "Too long," said Robo.

Robo looked at his drawing. The hero, the dragon, the pancake castle. He still could not think of a name. So he decided to play the game first. The hero flew over the pancake castle. The dragon slurped his soup. Then the dragon spilled the soup all over the castle, and the pancakes got soggy and started to slide!

Robo laughed out loud. "That's it!" he said. He wrote the name on the case in big letters: SOUPER PANCAKE PANIC. It was perfect. Everyone wanted to play it.

title: Pickle Ripple Surprise
story:
King Gloop opened the Ice Cream Flavor Lab. He wanted to invent the most amazing ice cream flavor ever. He scooped in chocolate. Then strawberry. Then, because he loved surprises, he added... pickles! He mixed it all together and called it Pickle Ripple Surprise.

He tasted it. His face twisted up. "Hmm," he said. "That might be TOO surprising." At the pretend ice cream shop, nobody ordered it. They all ordered vanilla. King Gloop sighed.

Then Duke Googool came in. "I'd like something unusual, please," he said. "Something no one else would ever try." King Gloop's eyes lit up. He scooped a big cone of Pickle Ripple Surprise. Duke Googool tasted it. He thought. He tasted again.

"Remarkable!" said Duke Googool. "Truly one of a kind!" From then on, Pickle Ripple Surprise was on the menu every day. Only one customer ever ordered it. But that customer came back every single day, and that made King Gloop very happy.

title: King Gloop's Surprised Face
story:
King Gloop knew a big surprise was coming. And he wanted to have the perfect surprised face ready. He stood in front of the mirror. He opened his mouth wide. "Oh!" Hmm. Too small. He opened it wider. "OHHH!" Now his crown fell off.

Baby Gloop giggled. "Papa, what are you doing?" "Practicing my surprised face," said King Gloop. "I want to look surprised enough."

Baby Gloop tried too. She made her eyes very round. She made her mouth a tiny O. Then she put her hands on her cheeks. "Like this?" King Gloop tried it. They both looked so silly that they started laughing. Then Robo came in and tried it too. His blue eyes went wide, and his antenna stood straight up.

They practiced all afternoon. Wide-eyed faces. Gasping faces. Faces that said, "No way!" But when the big surprise finally came, King Gloop forgot all about practicing. He was just really, truly surprised. And that face was the best one of all.

title: Too Many Clues
story:
Duke Googool was in charge of the clues for the family's surprise hunt. He loved clues. So he made a lot of them. He hid clues in shoes, in drawers, in flowerpots and under rugs.

Robo found one. It said, "Go to the shoe." The shoe said, "Go to the drawer." The drawer said, "Go back to the shoe." Robo went round and round in circles. "Duke Googool," said Robo, very dizzy. "I think we're lost."

Duke Googool looked at his giant pile of clue notes. "Oh dear," he said. "I may have made it a bit too twisty."

So they sat down together and picked the five very best clues. A riddle. A secret code. A treasure map. A silly rhyme. And one hidden under Sammy, who would not move. The new hunt was just right. It was tricky but fun. And at the end of it, the mystery box was waiting, with a big question mark on top.

title: Mimo Hides It Too Well
story:
The family's mystery box needed a good hiding spot until the big day. "I'll hide it," said Mimo the black cat. "Nobody is better at hiding than me." Mimo pushed the box into a very secret place. Then Mimo took a long nap.

When Mimo woke up, it was time to bring out the surprise. But Mimo could not remember where the box was! Mimo had hidden it too well. "Don't worry," said Rocky. "We'll help." So all four cats searched. Sammy checked the laundry basket. Jimmy checked behind the couch, grumbling. Rocky checked outside, under the porch.

Nothing. Then Sammy had an idea. "Mimo, show us where you like to hide." Mimo walked to the hall closet, slipped behind the coats and squeezed into a little cozy gap. And there it was! The mystery box, tucked safely in Mimo's favorite hiding spot.

"I found it!" said Mimo, with a happy slow blink. The cats pushed it out together. And Mimo took another nap right in the cozy gap.

title: The Burnt Batch
story:
Robo started his own Cookie Company. He invented Rainbow Sprinkle Cookies, Marshmallow Moon Cookies and a cookie with a tiny robot face. He put them in the oven and waited. Ding! But when he opened the oven, oh no! The cookies were dark brown and crispy. He had baked them way too long.

"They're burnt," said Robo sadly. "Now I have nothing to sell at the Cookie Shop." Then King Gloop came in. He picked up a crunchy cookie and dipped it into his glass of milk. The cookie got soft and yummy.

"These are perfect dunking cookies!" said King Gloop. Robo's blue eyes lit up. He made a new sign for his shop: "Super Crunchy Dunkers! Best with milk!" He put out a little cup of milk for each customer.

Everyone loved them. They dunked and munched and asked for more. The next day, Robo baked a new batch on purpose, extra crispy. And he set a timer, just in case.

title: The Pizza That Was Too Big
story:
King Gloop opened his own pizza place. It was called King Gloop's Royal Pizza. He made a pizza with cheese, olives and a crown made of peppers. But King Gloop got too excited. He kept stretching the dough. Soon the pizza was so big it hung off the table. It was as big as a rug!

Then it was time to put it in a box. But the pizza box was much too small. "Oh dear," said King Gloop. "I can't fit my pizza!"

Robo looked at the giant pizza. Then he looked at the little box. "What if we cut it into slices?" he said. "Then each friend gets their own little box!" They cut the giant pizza into slices. Each slice went into a small box with a lid that opened.

Then they delivered them, one by one. A slice for Baby Gloop. A slice for Duke Googool. The one big pizza turned into a party for everyone.

title: Sammy's Taste Test
story:
Sammy and Jimmy wanted to invent their own cat food. "It should be fish!" said Sammy. "No, chicken," grumbled Jimmy. They argued. Fish! Chicken! Fish! Chicken! Sammy's tail swished. Jimmy's ears went flat. Nobody was happy.

Robo came over with a can label and some crayons. "Why not try both?" he said. "We can have a taste test!" Sammy tasted a pretend bite of chicken. "Hmm. Not bad." Jimmy tasted a pretend bite of fish. "Hmph. Not terrible."

Then Robo mixed them together. Fish AND chicken. Sammy tasted it. Jimmy tasted it. Their eyes got big. They looked at each other. "Delicious!" they said at the same time.

So they named their cat food "Fishy Chicken Feast." Sammy drew a picture of himself on the label, saying, "Sweet freedom!" Jimmy drew himself next to Sammy, with his green eyes looking proud. They watched their TV commercial together, squished side by side on one cushion. And for the rest of the day, nobody argued at all.

title: The Lunchbox That Was All Cookies
story:
Baby Gloop was packing her very own lunchbox. She put in a cookie. Then another cookie. Then a cookie, a cookie and a cookie. "There," she said proudly. "All done!"

Robo peeked inside. "That's a lot of cookies," he said. "Where are your vegetables?" Baby Gloop made a face. "Vegetables are boring."

Robo thought about it. "What if they weren't boring?" He took a carrot and cut it into the shape of a rocket. He took a cucumber and made it into a little race car with grape wheels. He made a sandwich shaped like a star. Baby Gloop's eyes went wide. "Can I eat the rocket?" "Of course," said Robo.

So they packed the lunchbox again. A rocket carrot. A cucumber race car. A star sandwich. Some apple slices. And one cookie, right in the middle, like a treasure. At lunchtime, Baby Gloop ate everything, even the race car. Then she found a little note under her cookie. It said, "Have a great day! Love, Robo."

title: Down the Big Ramp
story:
Robo designed a race kart. It was blue with silver stripes and a little antenna on top, just like him. He folded it out of paper and set it at the top of the big ramp. His friends lined up their karts too. King Gloop had a purple kart with a crown. Baby Gloop had a tiny pink one.

"Ready, set, GO!" They let go of their karts. Whoosh! Down the ramp they went. But Baby Gloop's kart was very light. It went a little way, then tipped over and stopped. Baby Gloop's lip wobbled. "My kart is too small."

Robo picked up her kart. "Maybe it just needs a little weight," he said. He taped a coin to the bottom. "Try again!" Baby Gloop set her kart at the top. Ready, set, GO! This time the kart zoomed straight down. It passed King Gloop. It even passed Robo!

"I WON!" cheered Baby Gloop. Robo clapped. And that coin became her lucky kart coin forever.

title: The Question Mark Parade
story:
All around the Game Factory, there were question marks. There was one on a balloon. One on a sticker. One on a cloud. They had been showing up for a long, long time. One morning, Robo had an idea. "Let's gather them all together!"

So everyone brought their question marks. Baby Gloop brought her sticker. Rocky brought a question mark leaf. Sparks carried the balloon in his teeth, with Charlie and August waving from his back. They lined up in a long row. Then they marched! Jimmy walked at the back, saying he did not like parades, but he walked in perfect time.

The parade went all the way around the Game Factory. At the end, they put all the question marks in one big pile. When they stood back to look, the pile made one giant question mark, the biggest ever.

"What does it mean?" asked Baby Gloop. Robo smiled. "It means the best surprises are worth waiting for."

title: Rocky and the Shy Butterfly
story:
Rocky the gray tabby loved being outside. He loved the warm grass, the tall trees and the buzzing bugs. Most of all, he loved chasing butterflies. One sunny morning, Rocky saw a beautiful blue butterfly. He crouched down. Then he pounced! But the butterfly flew away, up into the Big Tree.

Rocky climbed after it, branch by branch. But every time he got close, the butterfly fluttered higher. "Why won't you play with me?" Rocky asked. "Because you keep pouncing," said a quiet voice. It was Mimo, the black cat, sitting on a branch nearby. "Butterflies are shy. Try sitting very, very still."

Rocky did not think that would work. But he tried it anyway. He sat on the branch. He just breathed slowly and watched the leaves. Then, very gently, the blue butterfly floated down and landed right on Rocky's nose.

Rocky's eyes went wide. He didn't move a whisker. "Hello," he whispered. Mimo smiled. It was the best game of all.

title: Robo's Costume Day
story:
Baby Gloop wanted to be a robot, just like Robo. So Robo helped her build Wear-It Robo Gear. They made a paper helmet with a big antenna. They even made a paper control panel with buttons to wear on her tummy. Baby Gloop put it all on. "Beep boop!" she said. "I am Robo-Gloop!"

But then she tried to dance, and her helmet slid down over her eyes. She tried to wave, and an arm band fell off. "Being a robot is hard," she said. Robo laughed kindly. "Let's fix it," he said. He added a soft strap under the helmet. He used a bit more tape on the arm bands. Then he turned on the Robot Voice Box. Now when Baby Gloop talked, she sounded just like a real robot!

"BEEP BOOP. I. LOVE. DANCING," she said in her robot voice. They turned on the Dance Party music. Robo and Robo-Gloop did the robot dance together, until they both fell over giggling.

title: Let It Rip!
story:
It was the big Spinning Top Battle! Everyone had designed a paper top. Robo's top was blue and silver. King Gloop's top was purple, with gold stars. Baby Gloop's top was very small and very pink. "Three, two, one, LET IT RIP!" shouted the announcer.

The tops spun around and around. King Gloop's big top wobbled into Robo's. Clack! Robo's top went flying. King Gloop's top spun on, slower and slower, until it bumped into the wall and fell over. But Baby Gloop's tiny top was still spinning. Round and round, in the middle of the arena, smooth and steady.

"How is it still going?" asked King Gloop. Baby Gloop smiled. "I made it small, and I put the stick right in the very middle," she said. "So it doesn't wobble."

Everyone was amazed. The stopwatch kept ticking. Ten seconds. Twenty seconds. Thirty! When her top finally stopped, everyone cheered. Baby Gloop was the Spinning Top Champion! King Gloop lifted her up on his shoulders, very proudly.

title: On Air!
story:
Robo built a paper TV out of a box. He put two pencils through the top and bottom, and drew a long paper strip that wrapped around them. When he turned the cranks, the pictures rolled by like a show! "Today's show is The Adventures of Super Sammy," said Robo. Everyone gathered around. The theme song played. Robo turned the crank.

Super Sammy flew over the city. Then... the paper strip got stuck! The crank would not turn. The show stopped right in the middle. "Oh no!" said Baby Gloop. "What happens next?"

Robo tugged gently, but the strip was jammed. Then King Gloop had an idea. "Commercial break!" he shouted. He jumped up and did a silly commercial for Gloopy O's cereal. Everyone laughed and clapped.

While King Gloop danced, Robo fixed the strip. A little tape, a little smoothing. Done! "And we're back!" said Robo. He turned the crank, and Super Sammy saved the day. The audience gave a huge round of applause.

title: The Missing Flipper
story:
Robo built a real paper pinball table. It had bumpers that said DING, targets that said BONG and two flippers at the bottom. He rolled a marble down the table. Ding! Bong! Ding! The marble bounced all over. Then the marble rolled toward the flippers. Robo pressed the left flipper. Flip! It bounced the marble back up. He pressed the right flipper. Nothing happened. It had come loose!

The marble rolled right past it. "Oh no," said Robo. "Game over." Robo looked at the broken flipper. The paper had gotten soft from too much flipping. He needed something stronger.

Sammy padded over, carrying a popsicle stick in his mouth. He had found it under the kitchen table, and he dropped it right next to Robo.

"Sammy, that's perfect!" said Robo. He glued the popsicle stick inside the paper flipper. Now it was strong and sturdy. Robo rolled the marble again. Ding! Bong! Flip! Flip! The flipper worked better than ever. Robo got so many points that the scoreboard shouted, "JACKPOT!"

title: Shake It, Gently
story:
Robo built a talking vending machine. You put in a pretend coin, pressed a button, and a crazy snack slid out the door. "Thank you for your order!" the machine would say. Baby Gloop put in a coin and pressed B3, for Rainbow Pretzel Puffs. The machine whirred. The snack wiggled forward... and then got stuck! It hung right at the edge, not falling.

"My snack!" said Baby Gloop. King Gloop wanted to help. He grabbed the machine and shook it as hard as he could. But all the snacks inside got jumbled up, and the machine said, "Ouch, ouch, ouch!"

"Wait!" said Robo. "Let's try gently." He gave the machine a soft little nudge. The machine giggled. "That tickles!" Then plop! The Rainbow Pretzel Puffs slid right out the door.

Baby Gloop clapped. King Gloop looked a bit sorry. So he patted the machine gently too. "Apology accepted," said the vending machine. And it gave him a free snack.

title: The Rarest Prize
story:
Robo and Baby Gloop were cracking open surprise eggs on their silly unboxing show. "Welcome back to Egg-citing Eggs!" said Robo. Crack! Inside the first egg was a tiny paper car. Crack! A tiny paper Gloop. Baby Gloop wanted the rarest prize of all, the Golden Star. They cracked egg after egg. But no Golden Star.

Soon there was only one egg left. Baby Gloop held her breath. Crack! Inside was... a tiny paper teddy bear. "Oh," said Baby Gloop. She tried to smile, but she was a little sad.

Robo had an idea. He got some gold paper and folded a brand new egg. Inside, he put a little gold star he made himself. He wrote on it, "For my best show partner."

He handed it to Baby Gloop. "One more egg," he said. Crack! Baby Gloop found the Golden Star. She gasped and hugged it close. "This is the rarest one in the whole world," she said. "Because there's only one, and you made it."

title: The Stinkiest Perfume Ever
story:
Duke Googool opened the Stinky Smell Shop. He wanted to make the yuckiest pretend perfume in the world. He mixed in old socks. Then a splash of swamp water, a pinch of stinky fish and one rotten banana. He called it "Eau de Pee-Yew."

He sprayed a little pretend puff. The Smell-O-Meter went wobble, wobble, WOBBLE! The needle spun all the way to "SUPER STINKY!" Then King Gloop walked in, took one sniff and fainted onto the floor with a big gooey splat. "Oh dear!" said Duke Googool. "That was a bit too much!"

Robo fanned King Gloop with a piece of paper. Baby Gloop brought him a fresh flower to sniff. Slowly, King Gloop woke up. "My perfume was too stinky," said Duke Googool. "I'm sorry."

King Gloop sat up and laughed. "Too stinky? That's the funniest thing I've ever smelled!" So they made a big sign for the shop: "WARNING: May Cause Fainting." And everyone wanted to buy a bottle, just for the giggles.

title: The Monster Who Was Scared of Brushing
story:
Robo opened the Monster Toothpaste Company. His toothpaste had red, green and blue stripes. Monsters came from all around to have their giant teeth cleaned. A big hairy monster came in. Scrub, scrub, scrub! His teeth went DING! A slimy monster came in. Scrub, scrub, scrub! DING!

Then a small, fuzzy monster came to the door. But it would not come in. It hid behind the door, shaking. "What's wrong?" asked Robo gently.

"I'm scared of the toothbrush," said the little monster. "It looks too big and scratchy." Robo thought about it. He found the smallest, softest toothbrush in the whole shop. He put on just a tiny bit of toothpaste. Then he let the monster hold the toothbrush itself. "You can be the boss," said Robo. "Brush as gently as you like."

The little monster brushed very slowly. It giggled, because the bubbles tickled. DING! Its teeth sparkled. The little monster smiled the biggest smile ever, and Robo gave it a Monster Dentist certificate.

title: The Fortune That Was Blank
story:
At the Fortune Cookie Factory, everyone was cracking open cookies. Each one had a silly fortune inside, read out loud in a funny voice. King Gloop's said, "You will find a sock in an unusual place." Baby Gloop's said, "A duck will think you are very cool." Robo's said, "Today you will do a happy dance."

Then Jimmy cracked his cookie open. He pulled out the little paper. It was blank! There was nothing written on it at all. "Hmph," said Jimmy. "Even the cookie forgot me."

Robo looked at the empty paper. Then he had a kind idea. "Jimmy, this is the most special fortune of all," he said. "It means YOU get to choose what happens."

Jimmy thought about it. Then he took a crayon in his white paw and wrote: "You will have a long nap in a warm sunbeam." Everyone cheered. Jimmy acted like he did not care. But that afternoon, his fortune came true. He napped in the sunniest spot for three whole hours.

title: But Wait, There's More!
story:
Robo invented a silly gadget. It was called the Hat-o-Matic 3000. You pressed a button, and it put a hat on your head. Any hat! He decided to sell it on a TV infomercial. "Are you tired of putting on your own hat?" said Robo to the camera. "Try the Hat-o-Matic 3000!"

He pressed the button. The machine plopped a cowboy hat on his head. "BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!" He pressed it again. A party hat! Again. A chef hat! Again. A pirate hat! But then something went wrong. The Hat-o-Matic would not stop! A wizard hat. A crown. A bucket. A pancake! Soon Robo was wearing a tower of hats so tall it touched the ceiling.

"Help!" he giggled, wobbling.

Baby Gloop ran over and pressed the button one more time. This time, out came a giant sleepy hat that covered the whole machine. The Hat-o-Matic went quiet and stopped. Robo laughed, still wearing all his hats. "BUT WAIT," he said to the camera, "there's MORE... sleepy machines!"

title: The Arcade That Needed a Player
story:
Robo found a giant cardboard box. "Let's turn it into an arcade machine!" he said. They painted the sides with stars and lightning bolts. They made a marquee on top that said GLOOP-A-TRON. They added a paper joystick and some big round buttons. It looked amazing. But when they finished, they realized something. "How does it actually work?" asked Baby Gloop. "It's just a box."

Robo thought. Then he grinned. "It needs someone inside!" So Robo climbed into the box with a tablet. He propped it up behind the screen hole. Baby Gloop put a paper token in the slot.

"INSERT COIN. GAME START!" said Robo in his best arcade voice. The game lit up on the screen. Baby Gloop moved the joystick, and Robo made beeping noises every time she scored.

"You got the high score!" said Robo from inside the box. Baby Gloop jumped up and down. Then she wanted a turn inside the box too. So they took turns being the player and the machine, all afternoon.

title: Mission to the Moon Cookie
story:
Robo and Baby Gloop turned a big cardboard box into a rocket cockpit. They drew buttons and dials inside. They cut out a round window and colored the outside silver. "Mission Control, we are ready for launch!" said Robo.

King Gloop was Mission Control. He counted down. "Ten, nine, eight... three, two, one, BLAST OFF!" Robo and Baby Gloop shook the box and made rumbling noises. Rumble rumble WHOOSH! They pretended to fly past stars and planets. Then King Gloop said, "Uh oh! Your rocket is running out of fuel!"

Baby Gloop looked worried. "What do we do?" Robo looked out the window. "Look! A planet made of cookies! Maybe cookies are rocket fuel!"

They pretended to land. Then they climbed out of the box and found a real plate of cookies that King Gloop had put on the floor. "Fuel collected!" said Robo. They each ate one. Then they climbed back into the rocket. "Mission Control, we're full of cookie power," said Baby Gloop. "Flying home!"

title: The Drawbridge That Wouldn't Close
story:
King Gloop designed a castle. It had tall towers, a big flag and a crest with a purple crown on it. And best of all, it had a real drawbridge that went up and down. Every evening, King Gloop played his trumpet. Then he raised the drawbridge, so the castle was safe and cozy for the night.

But one night, the drawbridge got stuck halfway. It would not go up. It would not go down. "Oh no!" said King Gloop. Robo came to look. He saw that the rope had gotten twisted around the wheel. "We need someone small to fix it," he said.

Baby Gloop stepped forward. "I can do it!" She squeezed into the tiny gap by the wheel. Her small purple hands untwisted the rope,.

"Now try!" she called. King Gloop turned the handle. Creeeak! The drawbridge went all the way up. King Gloop gave Baby Gloop a tiny trumpet of her own. "You are now the Royal Drawbridge Fixer," he said. Toot toot!

title: Robo Meets Giant Robo
story:
Robo printed and folded a giant paper Robo. It was ten inches tall,. Its arms really swung back and forth. Robo stood next to it. "Hello, Giant Robo!" he said. Giant Robo just stood there. It was paper, after all.

Robo felt a little silly. But then he had an idea. "I'll be your voice," he said. He moved Giant Robo's arm in a wave. "Hello, little Robo!" he said in a deep, booming voice. Baby Gloop giggled. King Gloop came over too. Soon they were all playing. Giant Robo struck a superhero pose. Giant Robo gave Baby Gloop a gentle paper high five.

Then Robo tried to make Giant Robo bow. He bent it too far, and its head fell off! Plop.

"Oh no!" said Baby Gloop. But Robo just picked it up and put it back on with a bit of tape. "Good as new," he said in the booming voice. "Even giants need a little help sometimes."

title: The Pilot License
story:
Robo designed an awesome spaceship. It had long wings, three engines and a glass dome on top. He watched it spin in 3D. Then he flew it in Flight Mode,. Next, he printed the paper model. It sat on a little stand, ten inches long. "Now I need a pilot!" he said.

Baby Gloop jumped up and down. "Me! Me! Can I be the pilot?" But Duke Googool raised his monocle. "To be a pilot, one needs a pilot license."

Baby Gloop's face fell. "How do I get one?"

Robo smiled. "You take a pilot test!" He made up three questions. "What do you say before launch?" "Three, two, one, blast off!" said Baby Gloop. "What do you do if you see an asteroid?" "Swerve!" "And what is the most important thing for a pilot?" Baby Gloop thought hard. "Being kind to your crew!" "You pass!" said Robo. He printed her a pilot license with her picture on it. Captain Baby Gloop was ready to fly.

title: Come In, Robo!
story:
Robo and Baby Gloop each had a paper walkie-talkie. Robo was at Radio HQ, and Baby Gloop was out on a mission in the backyard. "Come in, Baby Gloop," said Robo, holding his walkie-talkie. "Your mission is to find something red. Over."

Baby Gloop looked around. A red flower! "Found it! Over," she said. "Great job! Next mission: find something that bounces. Over." Baby Gloop bounced herself. "Found it! It's me! Over." Robo laughed so hard his antenna wobbled.

Then Robo said, "Final mission. Find something... soft and orange." Baby Gloop searched and searched. Not the carrots. Not the pumpkin. She was starting to feel stuck. "Robo, I can't find it! Over." "Here's a secret code clue," said Robo. "It says hmph. Over." Baby Gloop giggled. She tiptoed to the porch. There was Jimmy, napping in the sun, soft and orange.

"Found it! Over," she whispered, very quietly, so she would not wake him. "Mission complete, Agent Gloop," said Robo. "Come home for cocoa. Over and out."

title: The Quiet DJ
story:
Robo made a pair of paper headphones. They fit his head perfectly, right over his ear pods. Then he went to the DJ Booth and stacked up beats. Boom. Boom-tss. Boom-boom-tss! Soon everyone was dancing.

But Mimo, the black cat, was sitting in the corner with its ears flat. The music was too loud for Mimo's sensitive cat ears. Robo noticed. He did not want anyone to feel left out. So he turned the music down, down, down until it was soft and gentle. Then he made a second pair of paper headphones, very small, just for Mimo.

"These are special," said Robo. "When you wear them, the music is just the right size for you."

Mimo put them on. The beat was soft and slow, like a purr. Mimo's tail started to swish. Then, for the very first time, Mimo danced. Just a little sway, side to side. Everyone cheered quietly. It was the best Game Factory Radio show ever.

title: Is It Snack Time Yet?
story:
Baby Gloop made a paper wristwatch. It had a big round face, with numbers all the way around and two hands that really turned. She wore it proudly on her wrist. "What time is it?" asked Robo.

Baby Gloop looked at her watch. The hands were pointing everywhere. "Um... it's purple o'clock?" Robo laughed. "Let me show you a trick," he said. "The short hand tells the hour. The long hand tells the minutes."

Baby Gloop practiced. She turned the short hand to the three. She turned the long hand straight up to the twelve. "Three o'clock!" she said. "Exactly!" said Robo. "And do you know what happens at three o'clock?" Baby Gloop thought. Then her eyes got very big. "SNACK TIME!"

From then on, Baby Gloop checked her watch every few minutes. "Is it snack time yet?" Not yet. "Now?" Not yet. "Now?" Finally, both hands lined up just right. Three o'clock! Baby Gloop ran to the kitchen. She had never been so good at telling time.

title: Say Cheese, Jimmy!
story:
Robo built a paper camera. You could look through it, press the button and pull a pretend photo out of the film slot. Click, whirr! He took a photo of King Gloop making a silly face. He took one of Baby Gloop doing a cartwheel. Everyone loved posing.

But Jimmy did not like having his picture taken. Every time Robo pointed the camera at him, Jimmy turned around. Robo only got photos of Jimmy's back. "Hmph," said Jimmy.

Robo did not push. He put the camera down and sat on the couch. Then, later that afternoon, he saw something lovely. Jimmy was curled up in a sunbeam, with Sammy right next to him. Their tails were wrapped together. They were both fast asleep, purring.

Robo picked up the camera,. Click. He pulled out the photo and pinned it on the wall. When Jimmy woke up, he saw it. He looked for a long time. Then, without a word, he slept right underneath it.

title: Game Over? No Way!
story:
Robo made a paper game console. It had a slide-in screen, cartridges and two big buttons. When he powered it ON, he could play Robo Catch! Robo let Baby Gloop try it first. In Robo Catch, she had to catch falling stars in a little basket. She caught one. Two. Three. Then a star fell too fast, and she missed it. "Game over," said the console.

Baby Gloop frowned. "I'm bad at this." "No way," said Robo. "You caught three! Last time I caught two." He handed it back. "Let's try again."

Baby Gloop tried again. Five stars! Then again. Eight stars! Each time she got a little better. She learned to watch the stars before they fell, and to move her basket early. Then, on her tenth try, she caught every star. All twenty! The paper console flashed: "NEW HIGH SCORE!"

Baby Gloop screamed with joy. Robo wrote her name on the gamer card, under High Score, in big letters. "See?" said Robo. "Game over just means play again."

title: Following the Star Paw Prints
story:
One night, Sammy woke up and saw something twinkly on the floor. It was a paw print, made of starlight! Then another, and another, all leading out the window. "Wake up!" said Sammy. Jimmy, Rocky and Mimo blinked their sleepy eyes. They followed the glowing paw prints across the yard, over the fence and up a hill.

There, sitting under the moon, was Tiger, the gentle star cat. Tiger sparkled from nose to tail. "I've been waiting for you," said Tiger. "I want to show you something." Tiger led them into a dream. But in the dream, the grumpy Cucumber King was blocking the path!

Tiger winked. "Ready?" Together, the five cats did a karate move. Hi-YA! Bonk! The Cucumber King tumbled away, rolling like a little green log. Then Tiger showed them the most beautiful view, full of stars. They all sat together, purring. When the cats woke up in their beds, there was still one tiny star paw print on the windowsill.

title: Robo's First Steps
story:
A long time ago, there was a brand new robot. He was white and round, with a dark visor and blue eyes. His name was Robo. When Robo tried to walk for the first time, his legs went wobble, wobble, wobble. He fell right over. Clunk! "I'll never walk," he sighed.

Then a tiny cleaning bot rolled up. It had a teal dome, an orange stripe and one big green eye. "I'm Dusty," it said. "Want some help?" Dusty swept a straight line on the floor. "Just follow my line," said Dusty. "One step at a time."

Robo took one wobbly step. Then another. Dusty rolled slowly beside him. Soon Robo was walking all the way across the room.

"I did it!" cheered Robo. He was so happy that he bent his knees and jumped. Boing! It was the very first Robo Jump. From that day on, Robo and Dusty were best friends. And Robo never forgot the little bot who helped him take his first steps.

title: Glint's Own Song
story:
Glint was a mirror robot. It could copy anything. When Robo hummed a song, Glint hummed the same song. When Baby Gloop danced, Glint danced the same dance. Everything Glint did was a copy. One day, there was going to be a big concert at the Game Factory. Everyone was going to play their own song. Robo would play the drums. King Gloop would sing.

"What will you play, Glint?" asked Robo. Glint was quiet. "I don't have my own song," it said. "I only know other people's songs."

Robo had an idea. He took Glint to a quiet room. "Close your eyes," he said. "Listen to the sound inside you." Glint listened. At first, there was nothing. Then, very softly, it heard a little ring. Ting. Ting-ting. It sounded like a glass bell.

Glint opened its eyes. "Ting-ting-ting," it sang. It was not anyone else's song. It was Glint's. At the concert, Glint played its glass-bell song. Everyone stood up and clapped the loudest of all.

title: The Cucumber King Says Sorry
story:
The Cucumber King was back in the cats' dreams. But this time, he looked different. He was sitting all alone, looking sad. "What's wrong?" asked Sammy.

"Nobody wants to be my friend," said the Cucumber King. "Because I used to be so grumpy." The cats looked at each other. Jimmy understood. Sometimes he was grumpy too. "Being friends is something you can learn," said Jimmy.

So the cats taught him. Rocky taught him to share his cucumber slices. Mimo taught him to listen quietly when someone else was talking. Sammy taught him to take turns on the dream slide. Then came the hardest lesson. "When you hurt someone's feelings," said Jimmy, "you say sorry." The Cucumber King took a deep breath. He turned to the cats. "I'm sorry I was grumpy," he said. "I'm sorry I chased you."

The cats smiled. "We forgive you," they said. The Cucumber King smiled the biggest green smile ever. And from that night on, he was the friendliest vegetable in dreamland.

title: Baby Gloop Skips Her Nap
story:
It was nap time, but Baby Gloop was not sleepy at all. So when King Gloop closed his eyes, she bounced right out the window. Boing! She bounced to Kart Party and drove a tiny pink kart. She bounced to the Candy Factory. She bounced to Pet Park, Castle Defense and even the Zombie Maze, where the zombies just waved hello.

Meanwhile, King Gloop woke up. "Where's Baby Gloop?" he cried. Robo and Duke Googool helped him search. They went to Kart Party. She had just left! They were always one step behind. At last, Baby Gloop bounced into Sparks's world. But now she was very, very tired. Her bounce got slower. And slower. She curled up on Sparks's soft back and fell fast asleep. Charlie and August drove gently so she would not wake up.

When King Gloop finally found her, he did not get mad. He just smiled, scooped her up and carried her home. Next nap time, Baby Gloop stayed put.

title: The Runaway Snow Machine
story:
The first snow of winter fell on the Game Factory. Everyone ran outside. Robo threw a snowball at King Gloop. Splat! King Gloop threw one back. Then Duke Googool turned on his brand new snow machine. "More snow for everyone!" he said. The machine went whirr, and snow puffed out.

But then it went WHIRRRR! Snow shot out faster and faster. Soon there was snow up to their knees. "It won't stop!" cried Duke Googool. Robo had an idea. "If there's too much snow... let's use it!" Everyone started rolling. Big snowballs, giant snowballs, the biggest snowballs ever. They stacked them up into a huge Snow-Robo, as tall as a house!

By the time they finished, the machine had run out of snow and stopped by itself.

Then they went sledding down Gloop Hill, whooshing and laughing. When they got too cold, they went inside and sat by the fire with mugs of hot cocoa. Outside, the giant Snow-Robo stood guard all night, smiling at the moon.

title: The Tent That Kept Falling Down
story:
Rocky and Mimo were camping in the backyard. They had a tiny tent, two sleeping bags and a flashlight. "This is going to be the best night ever!" said Rocky. But every time they put up the tent, it fell down. Flop! They tried again. Flop!

"Maybe we're not good at camping," said Mimo sadly. Then they heard a soft "Hoo." It was a friendly owl named Willow, sitting on a branch. "You need to pull the corners tight," said Willow. "And tie them to something strong."

Rocky tied one corner to a tree root. Mimo tied another to a big rock. They pulled the strings tight. The tent stood up straight and stayed! As the sky got dark, fireflies came out and glowed all around. The giant moon rose over the fence,. Then, ZOOM! A shooting star streaked across the sky.

"Make a wish," whispered Mimo. Rocky closed his eyes. He wished for more nights just like this one. Then the two friends fell asleep, snug inside their tent.

title: The Best Seat in the House
story:
Robo turned the living room into a movie theater. He named it the Robo-Plex. He printed tickets, folded popcorn buckets and hung up posters of Ben's movies. Everyone came. King Gloop. Baby Gloop. Duke Googool. Sammy and Jimmy. They each gave Robo a ticket and found a seat.

But there was a problem. Everyone wanted the middle seat on the couch! King Gloop sat there. Then Sammy jumped onto his lap. Then Duke Googool tried to squeeze in. Then Jimmy hissed. It was a big, wobbly pile. "Wait!" said Robo. "I have an idea." He grabbed all the pillows and blankets in the house. He made a giant cozy nest on the floor, right in front of the screen.

"Now EVERY seat is the middle seat!" he said.

Everyone climbed in. It was soft and warm. Baby Gloop snuggled next to King Gloop. Sammy and Jimmy curled up together. "Curtains up!" said Robo. The trailers played. The movie started. Everyone munched popcorn, and nobody fought about seats again.

title: A Trophy for Everyone
story:
It was family game night, and Robo had made paper trophies and medals for the winners. There was a big gold trophy for first place. A silver medal for second. A bronze medal for third. They played a race game, then a tossing game, then a guessing game. King Gloop won first place! Duke Googool came second. Robo came third.

Then they held the Awards Ceremony. Drum roll! Fanfare! Confetti! But Baby Gloop was sitting quietly. She did not win anything.

Robo noticed. He went to the craft table and got busy. Snip, snip, fold, glue. "And now," he announced, "a very special award!" Drum roll! "The Best Cheerer Trophy goes to... Baby Gloop! She cheered for everyone, all night long!"

Baby Gloop gasped. It was true! She had cheered louder than anyone. She climbed up on the podium. Everyone threw confetti. Then Robo made more trophies. Best Laugh. Best Snack Sharer. By the end of the night, everyone had a trophy, and everyone was smiling.

title: The Dino Who Was Too Loud
story:
Robo made a paper dinosaur puppet. It had big teeth, little arms and a mouth that went CHOMP when he squeezed it. "ROAR!" said the dinosaur. "I am Chompy!" Robo put on a Dino Show. Chompy stomped across the stage. He gave a mighty ROAR!

But in the front row, Baby Gloop covered her eyes. She was a little bit scared. The roar was too big and too loud. Robo saw her. He stopped the show. He thought about it. Then Chompy peeked out from behind the curtain, very slowly.

"Um," said Chompy in a tiny voice. "I'm sorry if I was too loud. I only roar because I'm excited to meet you." Baby Gloop peeked between her fingers. "Would you like to pet my nose?" asked Chompy. "It's very soft."

Baby Gloop reached out and patted the paper nose. Chompy closed his eyes happily. "That's nice," he whispered. For the rest of the show, Chompy did tiny, gentle roars. And Baby Gloop laughed at every single one.

title: The Robo That Danced Backwards
story:
Robo built a paper automaton of himself. When you turned the crank, little paper wheels inside called cams pushed the arms and legs. Robo turned the crank. But the little Robo did not jump. It danced backwards! Its arms went the wrong way, and its legs kicked out behind it.

"Oops," said Robo. "Something is wrong." He looked at it in x-ray mode. He could see every cam and stick inside. Then he spotted the problem. "I put the cam on upside down!"

King Gloop laughed. "But the backwards dance is so funny!" he said. Robo looked at the silly paper Robo kicking backwards. It WAS funny.

So he had an idea. He fixed the cam to make the jump. Then he built a second automaton with the cam upside down on purpose. Now there were two paper Robos. One jumped. One danced backwards. When he cranked them both at once, they looked like they were dancing together.

title: The Train Car That Came Loose
story:
Robo designed a paper train. It had a bright red engine, a blue passenger car, a yellow cargo car and a little green caboose at the end. All the cars hooked together. "All aboard!" said Robo, wearing his conductor hat. Baby Gloop, King Gloop and Sammy climbed aboard. Toot toot! The train chugged along the track.

But going around a big curve, the green caboose came loose! It rolled slower and slower, and then it stopped. Sammy was in the caboose, all alone! "Stop the train!" shouted Baby Gloop.

Robo pulled the brake. Then he walked back along the track. Sammy was sitting calmly in the caboose, licking his paw, not worried at all.

Robo looked at the hook. It had bent. He folded a new one, extra strong, and hooked the caboose back on. "There," he said. "Now nobody gets left behind." Toot toot! The train chugged home. Sammy sat on the very back of the caboose, waving his tail. "Sweet freedom!" he said, enjoying the breeze.

title: The Giggling Phantoms
story:
One night, the Game Factory's power went out. Everything was dark. "Don't worry," said Robo, turning on his flashlight. "I'll find the fuses and turn the lights back on." He crept down the dark hallway. Then he heard a strange sound. "Hee hee hee!" Two glowing eyes peeked out from behind a box. It was a Phantom Robo!

Robo's antenna shivered. But then he remembered: Phantom Robos were not mean. They were just shy and silly. He shined his flashlight gently, and the Phantom Robo giggled and floated away. Robo found one fuse under the stairs. But the last fuse was nowhere to be found.

Then the Phantom Robo came back. It was holding something. The last fuse! "Found it in the dark," it whispered. "We can see well in the dark."

Robo smiled. "Thank you, friend!" He put in all the fuses and flipped the BIG power switch. Click! The lights came on. And there were six Phantom Robos, waving shyly. Robo invited them all to stay for cocoa.

title: The Ghost Who Wanted to Ride
story:
Robo climbed aboard the creaky ghost train. Clackety-clack, it rolled into the haunted Game Factory. The tunnels were dark and full of silly ghosts saying, "Boo!" Robo held up his lantern. Whoosh! The ghosts giggled and floated away. This was fun!

But in the very last tunnel, one little ghost did not float away. It just floated beside the train, looking sad. "Why aren't you spooking?" asked Robo.

"I'm tired of spooking," said the little ghost. "I just want to ride the train. But ghosts aren't allowed." Robo looked at the empty seat next to him. He looked at the little ghost. Then he slid over. "Who says ghosts aren't allowed?"

The ghost's face lit up. It floated into the seat. It was Phantom Robo! Clackety-clack, they rode the whole track together. Phantom Robo screamed "Wheee!" on every hill. When the ride was over, Phantom Robo did not want to get off. So they rode again. And again. Phantom Robo had finally made a friend, and Robo had too.

title: The Scarecrow Who Was Ticklish
story:
In the moonlit pumpkin patch, the jack-o'-lanterns were glowing. Robo wanted to collect them for the Game Factory party. But there was a silly scarecrow standing in the middle. Every time the scarecrow turned around, Robo had to FREEZE. If the scarecrow saw him move, it would shout, "I see you!"

Robo tiptoed. Freeze! He grabbed a pumpkin. Freeze! He was doing great. But then a leaf floated down and landed on his nose. Robo's nose tickled. He tried so hard not to sneeze. "Ah... ah... AH-CHOO!" The scarecrow spun around. "I SEE YOU!"

Robo braced himself. But then the scarecrow sneezed too. "AH-CHOO!" The leaf had tickled him as well! Then he started to giggle. "Hee hee, I'm ticklish!" Robo laughed. "Me too!"

The scarecrow stopped spinning. "You know," he said, "this game is more fun with a friend." So the scarecrow helped Robo carry the pumpkins. And that night, the scarecrow was the special guest at the jack-o'-lantern party.

title: Light the Lighthouse
story:
Robo sailed his little boat to Fog Island. The fog was thick and gray. "I need to light the lighthouse," he said, "so everyone can find their way." He climbed onto the beach with his lantern. Then he heard a wobbly voice. "Arrr! Who goes there?" It was a ghost pirate, wobbling on the sand.

Robo held up his lantern. The ghost pirates squinted and wobbled backwards. "Too bright!" they giggled. Robo found a piece of a treasure map in a bottle. Then another under a rock. Then the last one stuck to a seagull's foot. He put them together and found the treasure. Inside was a big golden lightbulb!

Robo climbed the lighthouse stairs. He screwed in the golden bulb. FLASH! The light swept across the island and out over the sea.

The fog melted away. Below, the ghost pirates looked up, blinking. "It's beautiful," they said. "Now we can find our way home too." They waved goodbye to Robo, smiling their wobbly pirate smiles.

title: The Spider Queen's Missing Shoe
story:
Robo put on his headlamp and climbed down into the Creepy Crawly Cave. The walls glowed blue and green. Little critters scurried by. At the very bottom of the cave lived the Spider Queen. She had eight long legs and eight sparkly shoes. But today, she was crying.

"What's wrong?" asked Robo. "I lost one of my sparkly shoes," sniffled the Spider Queen. "Now I only have seven. I can't go to the cave ball with one bare foot!"

Robo turned his headlamp all the way up. He searched the cave. He looked in a puddle. He looked under a mushroom. "I saw something sparkly," said the bat, "up in that crack in the wall."

Robo climbed up and reached in. There it was! The eighth sparkly shoe, shining in his headlamp. The Spider Queen put it on and did a happy dance with all eight feet. Tap-tap-tap-tap-tap-tap-tap-tap! Then she invited Robo to the cave ball as her very special guest.

title: The Rainbow Day
story:
One morning, everyone at the Game Factory woke up in rainbow colors! Robo was striped red, orange and blue. King Gloop was green and yellow. Sammy had rainbow stripes instead of brown ones. "Sweet freedom!" he said, admiring his tail. "What happened?" asked Baby Gloop.

Then Chaos Nova floated down, the rainbow star with one big eye. "I sneezed," said Chaos Nova, a little embarrassed. "And my rainbow sprinkled on everyone." At first, everyone thought it was funny. But then the rainbow bosses appeared! A rainbow Cucumber King. A rainbow Lock Robo. They were all rainbow too, and very confused.

"We don't know who we are anymore," they said. Robo had an idea. "Let's play a game! Everyone show what makes you YOU." Sammy shouted, "Sweet freedom!" Jimmy said, "Hmph." King Gloop wobbled. Robo did his famous Robo Jump.

Soon everyone remembered. Colors were just colors. What made them special was inside. By evening, the rainbow faded away. But everyone agreed: it had been the most colorful, happy day ever.
